ui.dialog.title: Method and sources
ui.dialog.intro: An independent reinterpretation of the idea behind Scale of the Universe by Cary and Michael Huang. Graphics, text, code and music are original; all that remains of the source work is the list of objects, which are facts.
ui.dialog.experiment: The whole project is an experiment to try Claude Fable 5.2, Anthropic's model. The model wrote the code and the text, researched and checked the data and chose the images on its own, starting from Federico Calicchia's requests. No person has reviewed the result: the site is published as the model produced it, and it may contain errors.
ui.dialog.translation: Italian is the original language of this site. The other languages are automatic translations, not reviewed by native speakers: if you find a mistake, please report it.
ui.dialog.contents.title: What it contains
ui.dialog.contents.count: {n} objects: {kept} of the 315 in the 2012 list, of which {r} with a value changed by more than 10%, plus {new} objects that were not there then.
ui.dialog.flag.r: The object is in the 2012 list, but the value here differs from the 2012 value by more than 10%.
ui.dialog.flag.i: predicted by a theory or used as a thought experiment, never observed.
ui.dialog.flag.u: measurement that is disputed or has wide margins of error.
ui.dialog.sizes.title: How to read the sizes
ui.dialog.sizes.body: Each object is drawn to scale at its diameter or its greatest extent. Elementary particles are pointlike as far as we know: their positions are conventions inherited from the original and are marked as uncertain. Cosmological distances are comoving, except where stated. The illustrations are schematic and indicative: where there is no photograph, the real shape of the object is not reproduced.
ui.dialog.sources.title: Main sources
ui.dialog.sources.intro: {verified} objects out of {n} have a value checked against an open, cited source, mostly space agencies, metrology institutes, databases, scientific papers and encyclopaedias. The source of each value, with the date of the last check, is on the object's card.
ui.dialog.diff.title: How it differs from the original
ui.dialog.diff.intro: The original is Scale of the Universe 2 by Cary and Michael Huang (2012). This edition takes up its idea and its list of objects, and changes the rest:
ui.dialog.diff.values: {r} values from the 2012 list have been corrected or updated; each card gives the source of the current value.
ui.dialog.diff.new: {new} objects were not in the 2012 list: recent discoveries and measurements, and objects added to fill gaps in the scale.
ui.dialog.diff.flags: Every hypothetical object ({i}) or one with an uncertain measurement ({u}) is marked as such, instead of being shown as a fact.
ui.dialog.diff.art: Graphics, text, code and music were redone from scratch: nothing from the original work was copied.
ui.dialog.diff.open: The code and data are public and reusable: code under the MIT licence, original text and illustrations under the CC BY 4.0 licence.
ui.dialog.images.title: Images
ui.dialog.images.intro: {photos} objects have a third-party photograph, used under a free licence (public domain, CC0, CC BY or CC BY-SA): author and licence are on the object's card. The other {art} have an original illustration, drawn for this site and reusable under the CC BY 4.0 licence, because for those objects there is no photograph, or no free and safe one.
ui.dialog.ui.title: Interface sources
ui.dialog.ui.concept: The idea of a continuous zoom by powers of ten: Scale of the Universe by Cary and Michael Huang; the same idea is known from the film Powers of Ten by Charles and Ray Eames (1977).
ui.dialog.ui.type: Typefaces: Fraunces and Public Sans (SIL Open Font License), served by this site itself: no requests to external servers.
ui.dialog.ui.art: On the canvas, objects without a photograph appear with their illustration or as drawings generated by the code of this page. The background is generated too: its colour follows the scale and grows darker towards cosmic sizes; each circle marks a power of ten.
ui.dialog.ui.music: Music: generated in real time by the browser with the Web Audio API; its timbre changes with the scale and it uses no recordings.
ui.dialog.ui.stack: Site built with Astro and UnoCSS, published on GitHub Pages.
ui.dialog.privacy.title: Privacy
ui.dialog.privacy.body: This site uses no cookies and tracks nothing: no analytics, no third-party services, no data sent to anyone. The only thing remembered is the language you choose, and it stays in your browser. The site is hosted on GitHub Pages, which, like any server, receives the IP address of its visitors according to its own policy.
ui.dialog.author: A project by Federico Calicchia.

ui.diff.updated.intro: All objects present in both lists. The 2012 value comes from the data of the original site. The dot marks those that differ by more than 10%: below that threshold the difference is mostly the rounding of the original, which gives one or two significant figures.

ui.diff.flagged.intro: Objects predicted by a theory but never observed, and measurements that are disputed or have wide error bars: here they are marked, not shown as facts.

ui.diff.removed.body: Three objects from the 2012 list are not here: the match, removed because no reliable source was found for its length; the Washington Monument and the Statue of Liberty, which were already missing from the draft this project started from.

schiuma-quantistica.name: Quantum foam
schiuma-quantistica.desc: Quantum foam is the hypothetical irregular, fluctuating structure that spacetime might have at extreme scales, of the order of the Planck length, about 1.6 × 10⁻³⁵ m. It has never been observed, and the size shown is a convention, not a measurement. In 2015, observations of distant quasars with the Chandra, Fermi and VERITAS telescopes ruled out two of the proposed models.

stringa.name: String
stringa.desc: In string theory, elementary particles are the vibration modes of one-dimensional objects, the strings. If the theory is to describe gravity as well, their characteristic length is of the order of the Planck length, about 10⁻³⁵ m. To date there is no experimental data confirming it, and the size shown is a convention.

lunghezza-di-planck.name: Planck length
lunghezza-di-planck.desc: The Planck length is one of the fundamental physical constants tabulated by CODATA. The value recommended in 2022 is 1.616255×10⁻³⁵ m, with a relative uncertainty of about 1.1×10⁻⁵. The charge radius of the proton is about 5×10¹⁹ times larger.

yoctometro.name: Yoctometre
yoctometro.desc: The yoctometre is 10⁻²⁴ m, that is, a millionth of a billionth of a billionth of a metre. The prefix yocto was adopted by the General Conference on Weights and Measures in 1991. The Planck length corresponds to about 1.6×10⁻¹¹ yoctometres.

neutrino.name: Neutrino
neutrino.desc: The neutrino is an elementary particle with no electric charge and no measured size: the value shown is a conventional position. It is the lightest of the known particles that have mass. The KATRIN experiment, with 259 days of data, set an upper limit of 0.45 eV on its mass at 90% confidence.

quark-top.name: Top quark
quark-top.desc: The top quark is the heaviest known elementary particle. The average of the direct measurements compiled by the Particle Data Group gives a mass of 172.60 ± 0.27 GeV. It has no measured size, and the value shown is a convention.

zeptometro.name: Zeptometre
zeptometro.desc: The zeptometre is 10⁻²¹ m, a thousandth of an attometre. The prefix zepto was adopted by the General Conference on Weights and Measures in 1991. At maximum sensitivity, the LIGO interferometers detect changes in the distance between the mirrors equal to one ten-thousandth of the width of a proton, that is, of the order of a hundred zeptometres.

preone.name: Preon
preone.desc: Preons are hypothetical constituents of quarks and leptons, never observed. Searches for contact interactions at accelerators have found no sign of an internal structure and set the compositeness scale above 24 TeV for the electron-quark channel. This corresponds to distances below about 10⁻²⁰ m, so the size shown is only a convention.

neutrino-ad-alta-energia.name: High-energy neutrino
neutrino-ad-alta-energia.desc: On 13 February 2023 the ARCA detector of the KM3NeT neutrino telescope recorded an event consistent with a neutrino of about 220 PeV. According to the collaboration, the event, named KM3-230213A, is the most energetic neutrino ever observed. The size shown is a convention, because a neutrino has no measured radius.

quark-bottom.name: Bottom quark
quark-bottom.desc: The bottom quark is a third-generation quark with electric charge −1/3 and a mass of about 4.19 GeV in the scheme used by the Particle Data Group. It was discovered at Fermilab in 1977, when the E288 experiment observed the upsilon particle, a bound state of a bottom quark and its antiquark. It has no measured size, and the value shown is a convention.

lunghezze-sondate-da-lhc.name: Lengths probed by the LHC
lunghezze-sondate-da-lhc.desc: Since 2022 CERN's Large Hadron Collider has been colliding protons at the record energy of 13.6 TeV. The smallest distance that can be explored depends on the energy exchanged between the constituents of the protons: estimates range from about 10⁻¹⁹ m, for energies of a few TeV, to about 1.5 × 10⁻²⁰ m if the whole collision energy is considered. The value shown is therefore an order of magnitude and not a measurement.

sensibilita-di-ligo.name: LIGO sensitivity
sensibilita-di-ligo.desc: LIGO is a pair of L-shaped laser interferometers with arms 4 km long, built to detect gravitational waves. It can measure a change in the length of the arms smaller than one ten-thousandth of the diameter of a proton, that is, about 10⁻¹⁹ m. With this sensitivity it recorded the first gravitational-wave signal in 2015, announced in 2016.

quark-charm.name: Charm quark
quark-charm.desc: The charm quark belongs to the second generation of quarks, has electric charge +2/3 and a mass of about 1.273 GeV according to the Particle Data Group. It has no measured size: the magnitude shown is a convention. The ZEUS experiment at HERA established that any structure of quarks is smaller than 0.43×10⁻¹⁸ m.

quark-strange.name: Strange quark
quark-strange.desc: The strange quark belongs to the second generation of quarks, has electric charge −1/3 and a mass of about 93.5 MeV according to the Particle Data Group. It has no measured size: the magnitude shown is a convention. The ZEUS experiment at HERA established that any structure of quarks is smaller than 0.43×10⁻¹⁸ m.

limite-sul-raggio-dei-quark.name: Limit on the quark radius
limite-sul-raggio-dei-quark.desc: This is the upper limit on the effective radius of quarks obtained by the ZEUS collaboration from electron-proton collisions at the HERA accelerator in Hamburg. The analysis, published in 2016 on data corresponding to about 1 fb⁻¹ of luminosity, sets the limit at 0.43×10⁻¹⁸ m with a confidence level of 95%. If quarks have an internal structure, it is smaller than this.

attometro.name: Attometre
attometro.desc: The attometre is 10⁻¹⁸ m, a thousandth of a femtometre. The prefix atto was adopted by the General Conference on Weights and Measures in 1964. It is the scale at which any size of quarks is sought: the ZEUS experiment at the HERA collider set an upper limit of 0.43 attometres on their effective radius.

quark-up.name: Up quark
quark-up.desc: The up quark has electric charge +2/3 and a mass of about 2.16 MeV according to the Particle Data Group. Together with the down quark it forms the first generation, the one all stable matter is made of. It has no measured size: the magnitude shown is the upper limit from the ZEUS experiment at HERA, according to which any structure has a radius smaller than 0.43×10⁻¹⁸ m.

quark-down.name: Down quark
quark-down.desc: The down quark has electric charge −1/3 and a mass of about 4.70 MeV according to the Particle Data Group, a little more than twice that of the up quark. Together with the up quark it forms the first generation, the one all stable matter is made of. It has no measured size: the magnitude shown is the upper limit from the ZEUS experiment at HERA, according to which any structure has a radius smaller than 0.43×10⁻¹⁸ m.

elettrone-limite-superiore.name: Electron (upper limit)
elettrone-limite-superiore.desc: In collisions between electrons and positrons, no internal structure of the electron has ever been observed. An analysis of data from the ALEPH, L3 and OPAL experiments at CERN's LEP accelerator sets an upper limit of 2.8×10⁻¹⁹ m on its size, with a confidence level of 95%. The electron therefore behaves like a point at least down to this scale.

raggio-d-azione-della-forza-debole.name: Range of the weak force
raggio-d-azione-della-forza-debole.desc: The weak force acts only over very short distances because the particles that carry it, the W and Z bosons, are very heavy. Its range is estimated by dividing ħc by the mass energy of the W boson, 80.37 GeV: this gives about 2.5×10⁻¹⁸ m. That is less than one hundredth of the classical radius of the electron.

femtometro.name: Femtometre
femtometro.desc: The femtometre is 10⁻¹⁵ m and is the scale of atomic nuclei. It is also called the fermi, a name that NIST lists among those not to be used with the SI. The charge radius of the proton is about 0.84 femtometres.

protone.name: Proton
protone.desc: The proton is one of the two particles that make up atomic nuclei, composed of three quarks held together by gluons. It has no sharp edge: its size is taken as twice the root-mean-square charge radius, which according to CODATA 2022 is 0.84075 fm with an uncertainty of 0.00064 fm. The resulting diameter is about 1.68 fm, that is, 1.68 millionths of a billionth of a metre.

neutrone.name: Neutron
neutrone.desc: The neutron is the neutral particle of atomic nuclei, made of three quarks held together by gluons like the proton. Since it has no net charge, its extent is derived from the magnetic radius, which the Particle Data Group gives as 0.864 fm: twice that gives about 1.7 fm. Outside the nucleus it is unstable and decays with a mean lifetime of 878.3 seconds, a little under 15 minutes.

nucleo-di-elio.name: Helium nucleus
nucleo-di-elio.desc: The helium-4 nucleus, also called an alpha particle, is made of two protons and two neutrons. Its root-mean-square charge radius is 1.6785 fm according to CODATA 2022, so the conventional diameter is about 3.36 fm. The most precise measurement, 1.67824 fm, was published in Nature in 2021 by studying muonic helium ions, in which a muon takes the place of an electron.

deuterone.name: Deuteron
deuterone.desc: The deuteron is the nucleus of deuterium, the heavy isotope of hydrogen, and is made of one proton and one neutron. Its root-mean-square charge radius is 2.12778 fm according to CODATA 2022, for a conventional diameter of about 4.3 fm. Although it has only two nucleons, it is more extended than the helium-4 nucleus, which has four.

elettrone-raggio-classico.name: Electron (classical radius)
elettrone-raggio-classico.desc: The classical electron radius is a constant with the dimensions of a length, built from the charge and mass of the electron: it is 2.818×10⁻¹⁵ m according to CODATA 2022. The magnitude shown is twice that, about 5.64×10⁻¹⁵ m. It is a convention and not a measurement: in experiments the electron appears pointlike down to scales thousands of times smaller.

nucleo-di-cloro.name: Chlorine nucleus
nucleo-di-cloro.desc: Chlorine-35 is the most common isotope of chlorine, with 17 protons and 18 neutrons in the nucleus. A 2025 measurement with X-rays from muonic atoms, carried out at the Paul Scherrer Institut, gives a root-mean-square charge radius of 3.3335 fm, so a conventional diameter of about 6.7 fm. Chlorine-37, with two more neutrons, turns out to be slightly larger: 3.3445 fm.

nucleo-atomico-medio.name: Average atomic nucleus
nucleo-atomico-medio.desc: The nucleus is the centre of the atom, made of protons and neutrons. Nuclei measure a few femtometres: the diameter ranges from about 1.7 fm for a single proton to about 15 fm for gold, and 10 fm is a typical value for a nucleus of medium-to-high mass. Although it is ten thousand to a hundred thousand times smaller than the atom, the nucleus contains over 99.9% of its mass.

nucleo-di-piombo-208.name: Lead-208 nucleus
nucleo-di-piombo-208.desc: Lead-208 has 82 protons and 126 neutrons and is considered the heaviest stable nuclide. Its root-mean-square charge radius is about 5.506 fm, for a conventional diameter of about 11 fm. The neutrons extend slightly beyond the protons: the PREX-2 experiment at Jefferson Lab measured in 2021 a "neutron skin" 0.283 fm thick, with an uncertainty of 0.071 fm.

nucleo-di-uranio.name: Uranium nucleus
nucleo-di-uranio.desc: The uranium-238 nucleus contains 92 protons and 146 neutrons. Its root-mean-square charge radius is 5.857 fm, which corresponds to a uniform sphere about 15 fm in diameter. It is not a perfect sphere: experimental data indicate an elongated shape.

picometro.name: Picometre
picometro.desc: The picometre is 10⁻¹² m, a thousandth of a nanometre. The prefix pico has been among the SI prefixes since 1960. It is the suitable unit for atomic dimensions: the Bohr radius, the length scale of the hydrogen atom, is about 52.9 picometres.

raggi-gamma.name: Gamma rays
raggi-gamma.desc: Gamma rays are the electromagnetic radiation with the shortest wavelength and the highest energy. By convention NASA calls gamma all photons with energy above 100 keV, that is, with a wavelength below about 12 picometres; the value shown here, 1.3 picometres, corresponds to a photon of about 1 MeV. On Earth they are produced by radioactive decays, lightning and nuclear explosions.

lunghezza-d-onda-compton-dell-elettrone.name: Compton wavelength of the electron
lunghezza-d-onda-compton-dell-elettrone.desc: The Compton wavelength of the electron is a physical constant linked to the electron's mass. The CODATA 2022 recommended value is 2.42631023538 × 10⁻¹² m, that is, about 2.43 picometres. It is named after the Compton effect, in which a photon strikes an electron and loses energy.

risoluzione-record-di-un-microscopio-ele.name: Record resolution of an electron microscope
risoluzione-record-di-un-microscopio-ele.desc: Electron ptychography reconstructs the image of a crystal from the diffraction patterns of an electron beam. In a 2021 paper, Zhen Chen and colleagues obtained an instrumental blur of less than 20 picometres, that is, 0.2 Å. At this level the limit is no longer the instrument but the thermal agitation of the atoms in the lattice.

atomo-di-elio.name: Helium atom
atomo-di-elio.desc: Helium has two protons and two electrons. Its calculated atomic radius is 31 pm, so the diameter is about 62 pm, against the 106 pm of hydrogen derived from the Bohr radius (52.9 pm). The value depends on the definition: the covalent radius is 28 pm.

angstrom.name: Ångström
angstrom.desc: The ångström is 10⁻¹⁰ m, that is, 0.1 nanometres, and is a unit outside the International System. It is of the order of magnitude of atoms: the Bohr radius is about 0.529 ångströms.

atomo-di-idrogeno.name: Hydrogen atom
atomo-di-idrogeno.desc: The hydrogen atom is made of one proton and one electron. Its size here is twice the Bohr radius, the constant that sets the scale of the atom in the ground state: 52.9 pm, so about 106 pm in diameter. Bound in a molecule it turns out smaller: the covalent radius is 31 pm.

atomo-di-carbonio.name: Carbon atom
atomo-di-carbonio.desc: Carbon is the element with six protons, the basis of organic molecules. Its covalent radius in single bonds (sp3) is 76 pm, so the diameter is about 152 pm. The radius shrinks to 73 pm in sp2 carbon and to 69 pm in sp carbon.

raggi-x.name: X-rays
raggi-x.desc: X-rays are represented here by the Kα line of copper, emitted by X-ray tubes with a copper anode. The Kα1 component has a measured wavelength of 1.5405929 ångströms, about 0.154 nanometres, comparable to the distances between atoms in a crystal. Copper is the most common anode material in single-crystal diffraction.

legame-carbonio-carbonio.name: Carbon–carbon bond
legame-carbonio-carbonio.desc: The single bond between two carbon atoms is about 154 picometres long: in ethane the measured distance between the two nuclei is 1.536 Å. Chains and rings of these bonds form the backbone of organic molecules.

atomo-di-zolfo.name: Sulphur atom
atomo-di-zolfo.desc: Sulphur is the element with 16 protons. Its covalent radius is 105 pm, so the diameter is about 210 pm. The van der Waals radius, which measures the footprint of the unbound atom, is almost twice as large: 189 pm.

molecola-di-co2.name: CO₂ molecule
molecola-di-co2.desc: Carbon dioxide is a linear molecule: one carbon atom between two oxygen atoms, with C=O bonds of 1.162 Å. The distance between the two oxygens is therefore 2.32 Å. Its concentration in the atmosphere has passed 425 parts per million: in September 2026 the monthly average measured at Mauna Loa was 426.07 ppm.

molecola-d-acqua.name: Water molecule
molecola-d-acqua.desc: A water molecule is made of one oxygen atom and two hydrogen atoms, with O–H bonds of 0.958 Å and an angle of 104.5°. The diameter of about 2.75 Å used here is an effective value, that of the molecule treated as a sphere: sources give figures between 2.63 and 2.8 Å. The two hydrogen nuclei are only 1.51 Å apart.

gate-di-transistor-piu-corto.name: Shortest transistor gate
gate-di-transistor-piu-corto.desc: This is a transistor with a molybdenum disulphide channel in which the gate is the edge of a sheet of graphene, only one atom thick: 0.34 nm. It was presented in Nature in March 2022 by a group at Tsinghua University in Beijing; the previous record, from 2021, was 0.65 nm. According to the authors' simulations, the effective channel is 0.34 nm long with the transistor on and 4.54 nm with it off.

atomo-di-cesio.name: Caesium atom
atomo-di-cesio.desc: Caesium is an alkali metal with 55 protons. In the solid metal two neighbouring atoms are about 532 pm apart, which corresponds to a metallic radius of 266 pm; the covalent radius is 244 pm, more than three times that of carbon. The hyperfine transition of caesium-133, at 9,192,631,770 Hz, defines the second in the International System.

molecola-di-caffeina.name: Caffeine molecule
molecola-di-caffeina.desc: Caffeine (C₈H₁₀N₄O₂, systematic name 1,3,7-trimethylpurine-2,6-dione) is an almost flat molecule, made of two fused rings with three methyl groups. In the three-dimensional model calculated by PubChem the two farthest nuclei are about 0.76 nm apart, and 0.65 nm if the hydrogens are excluded. The size therefore depends on what is being measured, and if the electron clouds are counted too, the footprint is larger.

molecola-di-glucosio.name: Glucose molecule
molecola-di-glucosio.desc: Glucose is a simple sugar with the formula C₆H₁₂O₆, which in solution almost always closes into a ring. In this form the molecule measures about 0.86 nm along its major axis and 0.84 nm along its minor axis, van der Waals radii included.

nanometro.name: Nanometre
nanometro.desc: The nanometre is 10⁻⁹ m, a billionth of a metre. The prefix nano has been among the SI prefixes since 1960. In the silicon crystal the lattice parameter, that is, the side of the unit cell, measures about 0.543 nanometres.

fullerene-c60.name: Fullerene C₆₀
fullerene-c60.desc: The fullerene C₆₀ is a closed cage of sixty carbon atoms arranged like the seams of a football, with 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons. The molecule has a diameter of about 1.03 nm, while two diametrically opposite carbon atoms are 0.71 nm apart. It was discovered in 1985 by Harold Kroto, Richard Smalley and Robert Curl, who were awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1996.

nanotubo-di-carbonio.name: Carbon nanotube
nanotubo-di-carbonio.desc: A single-walled nanotube is a sheet of carbon atoms just one layer thick, rolled into a cylinder. The first ones, obtained in 1993 by an IBM group by vaporising carbon and cobalt together in an electric arc, all had a diameter of about 1.2 nm. The diameter varies from one nanotube to another depending on how it is produced.

alfa-elica-di-una-proteina.name: Alpha helix of a protein
alfa-elica-di-una-proteina.desc: The alpha helix is the most common spiral coil of a protein chain: each turn comprises 3.6 amino acids and advances by 5.4 Å. The backbone, without side chains, has a diameter of about 0.6 nm. The side chains stick out to the outside, so the overall width depends on the amino acids present, and the value of about 1.2 nm used here is a conventional estimate.

dna-spessore.name: DNA (width)
dna-spessore.desc: DNA is a double helix made of two strands paired through the nitrogenous bases. The diameter is 2 nm, uniform along the whole molecule, and each turn measures 3.4 nm and contains about 10 base pairs. The structure was worked out in the 1950s by Watson and Crick from the X-ray diffraction data of Rosalind Franklin.

fosfolipide.name: Phospholipid
fosfolipide.desc: A phospholipid is a molecule with a hydrophilic head containing a phosphate group and two hydrophobic fatty-acid tails. It is typically 2–2.5 nm long, that is, half the thickness of a membrane. In water these molecules spontaneously arrange themselves into a bilayer, the basic structure of cell membranes.

doppio-strato-fosfolipidico.name: Phospholipid bilayer
doppio-strato-fosfolipidico.desc: The phospholipid bilayer is made of two rows of phospholipids with the hydrophobic tails facing inwards and the heads facing the water. The thickness is about 5 nm: a DPPC bilayer measures 4.6 nm, while complete plasma membranes range from 5 to 10 nm. A red blood cell, about 8 µm wide, is roughly 1,000 times wider.

emoglobina.name: Haemoglobin
emoglobina.desc: Haemoglobin is the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen: it is made of four chains, two alpha and two beta, each with a haem group containing an iron atom. The molecule has a diameter of about 5 nm, with dimensions of about 6 × 5 × 5 nm. Predicting protein structure with AlphaFold earned Demis Hassabis and John Jumper the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

membrana-cellulare.name: Cell membrane
membrana-cellulare.desc: The cell membrane is the thin envelope that separates the inside of the cell from the outside environment. It is made of a lipid bilayer about 4 nm thick, crossed and coated by proteins that bring the overall thickness to typically 7.5–10 nm.

anticorpo-igg.name: IgG antibody
anticorpo-igg.desc: Immunoglobulin G is an antibody: a Y-shaped protein of about 150 kDa, with two Fab arms that bind the antigen and an Fc stem. Its maximum extent is about 15 nm: measurements in solution give 15–16 nm, those on a surface about 14 × 8 nm. The arms are very flexible thanks to the hinge region, so the shape changes continually.

gate-di-un-transistor-in-produzione.name: Gate of a transistor in production
gate-di-un-transistor-in-produzione.desc: In the so-called 2 nm chips, in volume production since late 2025, the name is a commercial label and does not measure any part of the transistor. Manufacturers do not publish the gate length: IBM's 2021 demonstration 2 nm chip had a gate of 12 nm, about two dozen atoms long. The 2022 IRDS roadmap expects the channel length to stop shrinking at around 12 nm.

luce-euv-per-litografia.name: EUV light for lithography
luce-euv-per-litografia.desc: EUV lithography prints microchip circuits with extreme ultraviolet light of wavelength 13.5 nm, almost at the border with X-rays. To generate it, a CO2 laser hits a fast-moving tin droplet with two pulses. According to the manufacturer ASML, these machines print the most complex layers of chips at the 7, 5 and 3 nm nodes.

circovirus-suino.name: Porcine circovirus
circovirus-suino.desc: Porcine circovirus is a single-stranded circular DNA virus that infects pigs. The virion of type 1 (PCV1) measures between 17 and 20.7 nm in diameter, that of type 2 about 20.5 nm. According to the ICTV, PCV1 and PCV2 are the smallest viruses able to replicate autonomously in mammalian cells.

ribosoma.name: Ribosome
ribosoma.desc: The ribosome is the complex of RNA and proteins that reads messenger RNA and assembles proteins. It typically measures between 20 and 30 nm: about 21 nm for that of the bacterium Escherichia coli, about 25 nm for that of mammalian cells. In the E. coli ribosome about two thirds of the mass is RNA and one third protein.

virus-dell-epatite-b.name: Hepatitis B virus
virus-dell-epatite-b.desc: The hepatitis B virus infects liver cells. The infectious virion, called the Dane particle, is a double-shelled sphere 42 nm in diameter. It contains a circular, partially double-stranded DNA genome of about 3,200 base pairs.

nanoparticella-lipidica.name: Lipid nanoparticle
nanoparticella-lipidica.desc: A lipid nanoparticle is the sphere of fats that encloses the mRNA of vaccines and carries it into cells. It measures about 60–100 nm in diameter and is made of four components: an ionizable lipid, a neutral phospholipid, cholesterol and a PEG-linked lipid. The Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna COVID-19 vaccines both use this technology.

ultravioletto.name: Ultraviolet
ultravioletto.desc: Ultraviolet is radiation with a wavelength shorter than visible light. According to the World Health Organization the UV region goes from 100 to 400 nm and is divided into UVA (315–400 nm), UVB (280–315 nm) and UVC (100–280 nm); other conventions extend it to shorter wavelengths. UVC is completely filtered out by the atmosphere, and about 95% of the UV reaching the ground is UVA.

sars-cov-2.name: SARS-CoV-2
sars-cov-2.desc: SARS-CoV-2 is the coronavirus responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic. The particles are roughly spherical, and in the first electron microscope images, published in 2020, the diameter ranged between about 60 and 140 nm. The spikes on the surface, 9 to 12 nm long, give the virion the look of a solar corona, hence the name of the family.

hiv.name: HIV
hiv.desc: HIV is the retrovirus that causes AIDS. Its particles, roughly spherical, have no fixed size: sources give from 80–100 nm up to an average of 145 nm, with individual virions between 120 and 200 nm in cryo-electron microscope measurements. The value of 120 nm used here is therefore indicative.

fossetta-di-un-cd-profondita.name: CD pit (depth)
fossetta-di-un-cd-profondita.desc: The pits of a CD are the tiny hollows that encode data along the spiral track of the disc. They are about 125 nm deep, that is, about a quarter of the wavelength that the 780 nm infrared laser has inside the plastic of the disc. So the light reflected from the pit and that reflected from the surrounding surface are half a wavelength out of phase and cancel each other, and the player tells the two levels apart.

limite-del-microscopio-ottico.name: Limit of the optical microscope
limite-del-microscopio-ottico.desc: Abbe's diffraction limit says that an optical microscope can distinguish two points only if they are farther apart than about half the wavelength of light. In practice the minimum distance goes from 200 nm for blue light to 350 nm for red. Super-resolution techniques such as MINFLUX locate molecules with a precision of 1–3 nm.

batteriofago-t4.name: Bacteriophage T4
batteriofago-t4.desc: Bacteriophage T4 is a virus that infects the bacterium Escherichia coli. It has an elongated head of 120 nm by 86 nm and a contractile tail of 140 nm, for an overall length of about 260 nm. Six fibres of about 160 nm are attached to the base of the tail, giving it the look of a lunar lander.

batterio-piu-piccolo.name: Smallest bacterium
batterio-piu-piccolo.desc: Mycoplasma genitalium is a bacterium of the mycoplasma group, which have a diameter of about 0.2–0.4 µm and are among the smallest bacteria. When it was sequenced in 1995, its genome of 580,070 base pairs was the smallest known for a free-living organism.

particella-piu-penetrante-per-un-filtro-.name: Most penetrating particle for an FFP2 filter
particella-piu-penetrante-per-un-filtro-.desc: A face-mask filter stops both large and very small particles well: in between there is a size that passes through most easily, called the most penetrating particle. By convention 0.3 µm is given, the size that the US agency NIOSH considers the hardest to filter. Measurements on electrostatically charged N95 filters, however, place it between 40 and 300 nm, often around 40–50 nm.

luce-viola.name: Violet light
luce-viola.desc: Violet is the colour with the shortest wavelength in the visible spectrum. The border with ultraviolet is conventional: NASA gives about 380 nm as the limit for the human eye, while other pages of its site start the visible at 400 nm, the value used here. At the other end is red, at about 700 nm.

luce-verde.name: Green light
luce-verde.desc: Green light around 550 nm falls where the human eye is most sensitive in good lighting conditions. The photopic luminous efficiency function V(λ) peaks at 555 nm. The candela, the SI unit of luminous intensity, is realised with a luminous efficacy of 683 lm/W at 540 × 10¹² Hz, equal to 555.016 nm in air.

luce-rossa.name: Red light
luce-rossa.desc: Red light occupies the longest-wavelength end of the visible spectrum, around 700 nanometres. According to NASA, the human eye typically perceives wavelengths between 380 nm (violet) and 700 nm (red). Beyond this limit the infrared begins.

mimivirus.name: Mimivirus
mimivirus.desc: The Mimivirus is a giant virus that infects amoebae. The capsid has a diameter of about 500 nm and is covered by a dense layer of fibres 125 nm long, for a total diameter of about 750 nm. Because of its outward appearance it was at first mistakenly identified as a bacterium.

micrometro.name: Micrometre
micrometro.desc: The micrometre is 10⁻⁶ m, a millionth of a metre. The old name micron is listed by NIST among those not to be used with the SI. A human red blood cell has a diameter of about 7.7 micrometres.

virus-piu-grande.name: Largest virus
virus-piu-grande.desc: Pithovirus sibericum is a giant virus with an amphora-shaped particle 1.5 µm long. It was isolated from a sample of Siberian permafrost more than 30,000 years old and described in 2014, when it surpassed in size the pandoraviruses, about 1 µm long. Its genome, of about 600,000 base pairs, is instead much smaller than theirs.

cromosoma-y.name: Y chromosome
cromosoma-y.desc: The Y chromosome is the smaller of the two human sex chromosomes and contains almost 2% of the cell's DNA. In metaphase, when it is most condensed, it is typically 2 or 3 µm long, but the measurement changes with the degree of condensation. Its complete sequence, 62,460,029 base pairs, was published only in 2023 by the Telomere-to-Telomere consortium.

escherichia-coli.name: Escherichia coli
escherichia-coli.desc: Escherichia coli is a rod-shaped bacterium, used for decades as a model organism in biology. A cell typically measures about 2 µm in length and 1 µm in diameter, with a volume of around 1 µm³. The dimensions are not fixed: cells that grow faster are also larger.

particella-di-argilla.name: Clay particle
particella-di-argilla.desc: In particle-size analysis, clay is the finest fraction of a soil. The ISO 14688-1 standard and the classification used in the United States set the same limit: clay particles are those with a diameter up to 0.002 mm, that is, 2 µm. The value shown is therefore the maximum diameter, and most particles are smaller.

mitocondrio.name: Mitochondrion
mitocondrio.desc: The mitochondrion is the organelle that produces most of the ATP, the molecule that supplies the cell with energy. In its classic rod shape it is typically about 2 µm long and about 1 µm wide, but in many cells mitochondria fuse into networks that extend for tens of micrometres. It keeps a small genome of its own, a legacy of the prokaryote it is thought to descend from.

cellula-di-lievito.name: Yeast cell
cellula-di-lievito.desc: Saccharomyces cerevisiae is the yeast used to make bread and beer. Its cells are almost spherical, with a diameter of about 4 µm in the haploid form and about 6 µm in the diploid one. It is a model organism of cell biology and was the first eukaryote to have its genome fully sequenced, in 1996.

nucleo-cellulare.name: Cell nucleus
nucleo-cellulare.desc: The nucleus is the compartment of the eukaryotic cell that holds the DNA. Its diameter typically ranges from 2 to 10 µm depending on the organism and cell type. In a human cell it contains about 2 metres of folded DNA.

cloroplasto.name: Chloroplast
cloroplasto.desc: The chloroplast is the organelle of plants and algae in which photosynthesis takes place. It has the shape of a disc typically 5 to 10 µm long. Like the mitochondrion, it has its own DNA and ribosomes.

cromosoma-x.name: X chromosome
cromosoma-x.desc: The X chromosome is one of the two human sex chromosomes: it has about 155 million base pairs, about 5% of the cell's DNA. In metaphase it is a few micrometres long, typically between 5 and 7 µm, but the measurement depends on the degree of condensation. In cells with two X chromosomes, one of them is inactivated in the early stages of embryonic development.

globulo-rosso.name: Red blood cell
globulo-rosso.desc: The red blood cell, or erythrocyte, is the blood cell that carries oxygen. It is a biconcave disc with an average diameter of 7–8 µm and, as it matures in the bone marrow, it expels the nucleus and most of its organelles. It stays in circulation for up to 120 days.

infrarosso-termico.name: Thermal infrared
infrarosso-termico.desc: Thermal infrared is the band in which objects at room temperature emit: by Wien's law a body at 20 °C has its emission peak at about 9.9 µm. NASA gives the region between 8 and 15 µm as thermal infrared. Infrared was discovered in 1800 by William Herschel, who measured the temperature beyond the red of the solar spectrum.

globulo-bianco.name: White blood cell
globulo-bianco.desc: White blood cells, or leukocytes, are the blood cells that defend the body. The diameter changes with the type: 10–12 µm for neutrophils, 6 to 14 µm for lymphocytes and 12 to 20 µm for monocytes. They are far fewer than red blood cells: typically 5,000 to 10,000 per microlitre of blood.

fibra-di-seta.name: Silk fibre
fibra-di-seta.desc: The thread that the silkworm emits to build its cocoon is made of two filaments of fibroin held together by a layer of sericin. Each filament has a diameter of 7–14 µm, while the double thread typically measures 15 to 26 µm. A single cocoon yields a continuous thread 600 to 1,500 metres long.

twip.name: Twip
twip.desc: The twip is a unit of measurement used in software to position elements on the screen independently of the monitor. It is one twentieth of a typographic point, that is, 1/1440 of an inch, equal to about 17.64 micrometres. About 567 fit in a centimetre.

fibra-acrilica.name: Acrylic fibre
fibra-acrilica.desc: Acrylic fibre is a synthetic fibre composed of at least 85% acrylonitrile by weight. The diameter depends on the linear density chosen by the manufacturer: with a density of 1.18 g/cm³, a 3-denier fibre measures about 19 µm and a 15-denier one about 42 µm. It does not melt, but decomposes above about 260 °C.

gocciolina-di-nebbia.name: Fog droplet
gocciolina-di-nebbia.desc: Fog is a cloud in contact with the ground, made of water droplets suspended in the air. Their diameter ranges from about 1 to 40 µm, as in clouds, but in fog the droplets are normally found in the lower part of this range. The value shown is therefore an order of magnitude, not a typical measurement.

thou.name: Thou
thou.desc: The thou, also called the mil, is a thousandth of an inch. It corresponds exactly to 25.4 micrometres, that is, 0.0254 millimetres. About 39 thou therefore fit in a millimetre.

cellula-della-pelle.name: Skin cell
cellula-della-pelle.desc: Keratinocytes are the main cells of the epidermis. They are born in the basal layer, where they measure 6–10 µm, and in about a month they rise to the surface, flattening into nucleus-free scales, the corneocytes. A corneocyte has a surface area of 700–1,200 µm², which corresponds to a diameter of about 30–40 µm.

particella-di-limo.name: Silt particle
particella-di-limo.desc: Silt is the fraction of a soil with grains intermediate between clay and sand. According to the ISO 14688-1 standard it comprises particles with a diameter between 0.002 and 0.063 mm, that is, from 2 to 63 µm. The classification used in the United States for agricultural soils instead sets the upper limit at 0.05 mm.

granulo-di-polline.name: Pollen grain
granulo-di-polline.desc: The pollen grain carries the male reproductive cells of seed plants. The size varies a great deal with the species: from about 10 µm in nettle to about 200 µm in silver fir. Even the same living grain swells and shrinks according to humidity.

pixel-di-uno-smartphone.name: Smartphone pixel
pixel-di-uno-smartphone.desc: The screen of a recent smartphone has a density of about 460 pixels per inch: this is the value Apple states for the iPhone 16, with 2556 × 1179 pixels on a 6.1-inch diagonal. At this density each pixel is about 55 µm wide, less than the thickness of a hair. That is why at normal reading distance the individual pixels cannot be told apart.

spermatozoo.name: Spermatozoon
spermatozoo.desc: The spermatozoon is the male reproductive cell. The human one is about 55 micrometres long in all: the head, which contains the nucleus, measures 4–5 micrometres, while the tail is about 50 micrometres long. Almost all the length is therefore due to the tail, the flagellum that makes it move.

capello-umano.name: Human hair
capello-umano.desc: A human hair is roughly 80 to 100 µm wide, according to the US National Nanotechnology Initiative. The thickness varies greatly from person to person and even between hairs on the same head. It is one of the most widely used points of comparison for microscopic sizes: it equals 80,000–100,000 nanometres.

limite-dell-occhio-nudo.name: Limit of the naked eye
limite-dell-occhio-nudo.desc: The limit of the naked eye is the minimum distance at which two nearby points are still seen as separate. The reference value used in microscopy is about 0.1 mm, that is, 100 µm, but it is a convention: it depends on each person's eyesight, on the light and on the contrast. A standard optical microscope reaches about 0.2 µm, five hundred times better.

foglio-di-carta-spessore.name: Sheet of paper (thickness)
foglio-di-carta-spessore.desc: A sheet of ordinary 80 g/m² printer paper is about a tenth of a millimetre thick. A manufacturer's data sheet gives 106 µm, with a tolerance of 3 µm, measured according to the ISO 534 standard. A ream of 500 sheets is therefore a little over 5 cm tall.

ovulo-umano.name: Human egg cell
ovulo-umano.desc: The egg cell, or oocyte, is the female reproductive cell. In a study of 1,563 human oocytes the mean diameter measured was 115 micrometres, with values between 60 and 171 micrometres. Its size is greater than that of the other cells of the body.

protista-ciliato.name: Ciliate protist
protista-ciliato.desc: Ciliates are single-celled organisms covered with cilia, which beat to propel the cell through the water or to bring food towards the mouth. About 7,000 species are known and the sizes vary greatly: paramecia typically range from 50 to 300 micrometres, while some genera reach 2 millimetres. The value of 180 micrometres therefore indicates only an intermediate size.

paramecio.name: Paramecium
paramecio.desc: The paramecium is a freshwater ciliate protist, used for over a century as a model organism in genetics and cell biology. The species of the genus are typically 50 to 300 micrometres long, and the largest, such as Paramecium caudatum, measure 170–310 micrometres, enough to be just visible to the naked eye. Like all ciliates, each cell has two types of nucleus.

pixel-di-un-monitor.name: Monitor pixel
pixel-di-un-monitor.desc: The reference density for desktop monitors is 96 pixels per inch: at this density a pixel is 1/96 of an inch wide, that is, about 0.26 mm. It is also the basis of the reference pixel used by the W3C to define the px unit in web pages. Today's phone screens, with about 460 pixels per inch, are almost five times denser.

acaro-della-polvere.name: Dust mite
acaro-della-polvere.desc: Dust mites are tiny arachnids that live in beds, sofas and carpets, where they feed on the skin flakes shed by people and pets. Sources give different lengths, from about a quarter of a millimetre up to about 0.5 mm for adults, so they can be seen well only under a microscope. Their droppings can cause or worsen asthma in sensitised people.

granello-di-sale.name: Grain of salt
granello-di-sale.desc: A grain of table salt is a small crystal of sodium chloride. In granulated table salt the grains typically measure 0.3 to 1.5 mm, and the one shown here is among the smallest. Pickling salt is more regular, with rounded cubes of about 0.5 mm.

ameba.name: Amoeba
ameba.desc: Amoeba proteus is a large single-celled freshwater organism that moves and captures food by extending pseudopods. It has no fixed shape: moving cells are typically 220 to 760 micrometres long, with an average of 425. It lives in fresh water and in wet sphagnum and is not a rare species.

tardigrado.name: Tardigrade
tardigrado.desc: Tardigrades are microscopic animals, on average 0.1 to 0.5 mm long, of which over 1,000 species are known. They can enter cryptobiosis, a state of suspended life. In this way they survive extreme conditions such as the absence of oxygen, vacuum and ionizing radiation.

granello-di-sabbia.name: Grain of sand
granello-di-sabbia.desc: In geology, sand is a loose sediment with grains between 0.062 and 2 mm in diameter. Sands are divided into five classes, from very fine (0.125–0.062 mm) to very coarse (2–1 mm). A grain of about 0.5 mm sits on the border between medium and coarse sand.

pelle-delle-palpebre.name: Eyelid skin
pelle-delle-palpebre.desc: The skin of the eyelids is about 0.5 mm thick. According to the University of Leeds histology atlas it is the lowest value in the human body, where skin thickness reaches 4.0 mm on the heels. It is thin skin, with four cell layers in the epidermis instead of the five of thick skin.

mina-di-matita.name: Pencil lead
mina-di-matita.desc: Leads for mechanical pencils are sold in fixed nominal diameters, and the one shown here is 0.7 mm. Manufacturers describe it as a fine lead, suitable for ordinary mechanical pencils, which draws a line about 0.7 mm wide.

carta-di-credito-spessore.name: Credit card (thickness)
carta-di-credito-spessore.desc: Credit cards follow the ID-1 format of the ISO/IEC 7810 standard, which sets a nominal thickness of 0.76 mm. The same format measures 85.60 mm by 53.98 mm. The standard specifies the same thickness for three other identification card formats, including the 25 mm by 15 mm ID-000.

millimetro.name: Millimetre
millimetro.desc: The millimetre is the thousandth part of a metre: the SI prefix milli stands for the factor 10⁻³. One inch is exactly 25.4 millimetres.

picco-del-fondo-cosmico-a-microonde.name: Peak of the cosmic microwave background
picco-del-fondo-cosmico-a-microonde.desc: The cosmic microwave background is the residual radiation of the Big Bang that fills the whole universe, formed about 380,000 years after it. Today it has the spectrum of a blackbody at 2.7255 K, whose peak per unit wavelength falls at about 1.06 mm. It is the farthest point back in time that can be observed with light.

goccia-di-pioggia.name: Raindrop
goccia-di-pioggia.desc: Raindrops do not have the teardrop shape of drawings. Those with a radius smaller than 1 mm are spherical, while the larger ones, as they fall, resemble the top half of a hamburger bun. According to NASA, a drop that grows to about 4 mm or more breaks up into smaller drops.

lenticchia-d-acqua.name: Common duckweed
lenticchia-d-acqua.desc: Common duckweed (Lemna minor) is a free-floating aquatic plant that forms green carpets on the surface of ponds and still waters. Each plantlet is a single oval frond 1 to 8 mm long, typically a few millimetres. It is among the smallest flowering plants.

seme-di-sesamo.name: Sesame seed
seme-di-sesamo.desc: The sesame seed (Sesamum indicum) is typically about 3 mm long and almost 2 mm wide. It contains about 50% oil and 25% protein. A thousand seeds weigh roughly 28 grams.

formica.name: Ant
formica.desc: Ants are social insects of the family Formicidae, with about 12,000 species described worldwide. The sizes vary greatly from one species to another: the worker of the common black garden ant (Lasius niger) is 3.5 to 5 mm long. The existing species are estimated to number about 15,000.

pelle-della-pianta-del-piede.name: Skin of the sole of the foot
pelle-della-pianta-del-piede.desc: Under the foot the skin reaches the greatest thickness in the human body: about 4.0 mm on the heels, against 0.5 mm on the eyelids. It is thick skin, found where abrasion is strong, that is, on the soles of the feet, the palms and the fingertips. Its epidermis has five cell layers instead of the four of thin skin.

nevischio.name: Snow grains
nevischio.desc: Snow grains are a precipitation of very small ice grains, white and opaque, flat or elongated. Their diameter is generally less than 1 mm. When they hit the ground they do not bounce or shatter, and they usually fall in small amounts from fogs or thick layers of cloud.

microchip.name: Microchip
microchip.desc: A microchip is an integrated circuit built on a tiny silicon die. There is no single size: the example here is a small 8-pin integrated circuit such as the NE555 timer, which in the SOIC package occupies 4.9 mm by 6 mm.

chicco-di-riso.name: Grain of rice
chicco-di-riso.desc: The length of a grain of rice depends on the variety. The scale of the international institute IRRI, reported by the FAO for brown rice, calls a grain short below 5.50 mm, medium between 5.51 and 6.60 mm, long between 6.61 and 7.50 mm and extra long above 7.50 mm. A 6 mm grain is therefore of medium length.

fiocco-di-neve.name: Snowflake
fiocco-di-neve.desc: A snowflake can be a single ice crystal or an aggregate of many crystals. According to the physicist Kenneth Libbrecht of Caltech, a good-sized crystal measures about 2 mm and an exceptional one reaches 10 mm, while the aggregates photographed by the meteorologist Sandra Yuter reach 35 mm. The value of 8 mm therefore indicates a large flake, not a standard measurement.

batterio-piu-grande.name: Largest bacterium
batterio-piu-grande.desc: Thiomargarita magnifica, described in Science in 2022, is the largest known bacterium: its filamentous cell is on average over 9,000 micrometres long, about a centimetre, and is visible to the naked eye. Most bacteria measure around 2 micrometres, and the largest previously known reached 750 micrometres. Its DNA is enclosed in membrane-bound compartments, which is unusual for a bacterium.

chicco-di-caffe.name: Coffee bean
chicco-di-caffe.desc: The coffee bean is the seed of the coffee plant, which is roasted before being ground. In a 2022 study of roasted commercial samples the mean length was 10.95 mm for the Arabica species and 10.46 mm for Robusta, with a width of just over 8 mm. The measurement changes with the variety, so about 1 cm is a typical value.

seme-di-girasole.name: Sunflower seed
seme-di-girasole.desc: The sunflower seed is actually a dry fruit, the achene, which encloses the seed proper. A study by Uludağ University measured on average 7.79 mm in length, 7.12 mm in width and 4.18 mm in thickness. The length depends greatly on the variety, and snacking seeds are noticeably longer.

uovo-di-colibri.name: Hummingbird egg
uovo-di-colibri.desc: The smallest egg laid by a bird is, according to the Guinness World Records, that of Mellisuga minima, a hummingbird that lives in Jamaica. Two specimens measured less than 10 mm in length and weighed 0.365 g and 0.375 g.

biglia.name: Marble
biglia.desc: The marble is a small sphere, today almost always made of glass, used in many children's games. The most common size is 5/8 of an inch, that is, about 16 mm, which is also the size set by tournament rules for target marbles. The oldest marbles were made of stone or clay.

penny-statunitense.name: US penny
penny-statunitense.desc: The penny is the United States one-cent coin and by law has a diameter of 0.75 inches, that is, 19.05 mm. The last one intended for circulation was struck on 12 November 2025 at the Philadelphia mint. Coins already issued remain legal tender.

moneta-da-1-euro.name: 1 euro coin
moneta-da-1-euro.desc: The 1 euro coin has a diameter of 23.25 mm, a thickness of 2.33 mm and weighs 7.50 g. It is bimetallic: the outer ring is nickel-brass, while the inner part is made of three layers of copper-nickel, nickel and copper-nickel. The edge alternates smooth and milled sections.

pollice.name: Inch
pollice.desc: The inch is an Anglo-American unit of length equal to exactly 2.54 centimetres. Twelve inches make a foot, equal to 0.3048 metres.

uovo-di-quaglia.name: Quail egg
uovo-di-quaglia.desc: The egg of the domestic Japanese quail, the kind found in shops, is typically about 32 mm long and about 25 mm wide. In a study by the University of Iași the mean weight was 10.44 g. The shell is light with dark spots.

uovo-di-gallina.name: Hen's egg
uovo-di-gallina.desc: A laying hen's egg is typically between 5.5 and 6 cm long and just over 4 cm wide. In a 2024 study of nine genetic types, the eggs of Lohmann Brown layers measured on average 56.12 mm in length and 43.32 mm in width, with a weight of 59.59 g. Smaller breeds lay eggs of about 51 mm.

cubo-di-rubik.name: Rubik's Cube
cubo-di-rubik.desc: The Rubik's Cube is a mechanical puzzle made of 27 small cubes, invented in Budapest by the design teacher Ernő Rubik, who assembled the first one in 1974. The edge measures between 5.5 and 5.7 cm or so: the specimen in the Victoria and Albert Museum in London is 5.5 cm high. Since 2014 it has been part of the National Toy Hall of Fame.

colibri.name: Hummingbird
colibri.desc: Hummingbirds are small American birds able to hover in front of flowers. The ruby-throated hummingbird, the most widespread in eastern North America, is typically 7.5 to 9 cm long and weighs less than 4 grams. Its wings beat about 53 times a second.

toporagno.name: Shrew
toporagno.desc: The common shrew is a small insectivorous mammal found across much of Europe as far as Siberia. Head and body typically measure 5 to 8 cm and the tail 2.5 to 4.5 cm, for a total of around 10 cm and a weight of 5–14 grams. It lives on average about two years.

tazza.name: Mug
tazza.desc: The mug is a cylindrical vessel with a handle, used for hot drinks. There is no standard size: the height typically ranges from 8 to 11 cm depending on the model, and for example the FÄRGRIK stoneware mug from IKEA is 11 cm tall and holds 25 cl. The value of about 10 cm is therefore indicative.

microonde-del-forno.name: Oven microwaves
microonde-del-forno.desc: Household microwave ovens operate at 2,450 MHz, which corresponds to a wavelength of about 12.2 cm. Microwaves make the water molecules in food vibrate, and this produces the heat that cooks it. The frequency falls in a band reserved for industrial, scientific and medical uses (2,450 MHz ± 50 MHz), the same region of the spectrum used by unlicensed 2.4 GHz radio devices.

smartphone.name: Smartphone
smartphone.desc: A current smartphone is typically about 15 cm tall. The iPhone 16, for example, measures 147.6 mm in height, 71.6 mm in width and 7.8 mm in thickness, with a screen of 6.1 inches diagonal. The dimensions vary from model to model.

uovo-di-struzzo.name: Ostrich egg
uovo-di-struzzo.desc: The ostrich egg is the largest laid by a living animal. It measures on average about 15 cm in length by 13 cm in width and weighs about 1.5 kg, roughly as much as 24 hen's eggs. Compared with the size of the adult, however, it is a small egg.

lombrico-comune.name: Common earthworm
lombrico-comune.desc: The common earthworm (Lumbricus terrestris) is an annelid worm native to Europe, pinkish to reddish-brown in colour. As an adult it is typically 10 to 25 cm long. It digs permanent vertical burrows that descend deep into the soil.

chicco-di-grandine-piu-grande.name: Record hailstone (USA)
chicco-di-grandine-piu-grande.desc: The hailstone that fell at Vivian, South Dakota, on 23 July 2010 measured 8 inches in diameter, that is, about 20 cm, and weighed about 0.88 kg. According to the National Weather Service it holds the United States record for diameter and for weight. The circumference record instead remains with a hailstone that fell at Aurora, Nebraska, in 2003.

pallone-da-calcio.name: Football
pallone-da-calcio.desc: The regulation football is a sphere with a circumference between 68 and 70 cm, which corresponds to a diameter of about 22 cm. According to the IFAB Laws of the Game it must weigh between 410 and 450 grams at the start of the match. The prescribed pressure ranges from 0.6 to 1.1 atmospheres.

pallone-da-basket.name: Basketball
pallone-da-basket.desc: The size 7 basketball, used in men's competitions, has a circumference between 750 and 770 mm, equal to a diameter of about 24 cm. The FIBA rules set its weight between 580 and 620 grams. In women's competitions the size 6 ball is used, a little smaller, with a circumference between 715 and 730 mm.

teiera-di-russell.name: Russell's teapot
teiera-di-russell.desc: Russell's teapot is a thought experiment proposed by the philosopher Bertrand Russell in 1952, in the essay "Is There a God?". Russell imagines a china teapot in elliptical orbit around the Sun between the Earth and Mars, too small to be seen even by the most powerful telescopes: nobody could prove that it does not exist, but that is no reason to believe in it. The argument concerns the burden of proof, and the size of about 25 cm given here is just that of an ordinary teapot.

righello-da-un-piede.name: One-foot ruler
righello-da-un-piede.desc: A one-foot ruler is exactly 0.3048 metres long, that is, 30.48 cm. The ratio between foot and metre was fixed this way in 1959. In the United States the old "survey foot", slightly different, has been declared obsolete since 1 January 2023.

uno-schermo.name: A screen
uno-schermo.desc: The screen of a compact laptop has a diagonal of about 34 cm: more or less the window you are looking through, if you are using a computer. The 13-inch MacBook Air, for example, has a screen of 13.6 inches diagonal, that is, 34.5 cm. Phone screens are much smaller and those of desktop monitors larger.

fiocco-di-neve-piu-grande.name: Largest snowflake
fiocco-di-neve-piu-grande.desc: According to the Guinness World Records, on the night of 27 January 1887 a storm dropped snowflakes described as "larger than milk pans" in the Clark Fork valley, near Missoula in Montana. Accounts speak of flakes up to 38 cm wide and 20 cm thick. This is a testimony from the time, not an instrumental measurement.

gatto.name: Cat
gatto.desc: The domestic cat (Felis catus) is a small feline weighing on average 4 to 5.5 kg. From the nose to the base of the tail an adult typically measures between 45 and 55 cm: in a study of 546 stray and feral cats in Australia the average was 50 cm for females and 55 cm for males. It probably descends from the African wildcat.

pallone-da-spiaggia.name: Beach ball
pallone-da-spiaggia.desc: The beach ball is an inflatable ball of light vinyl, usually with coloured panels. There is no standard size: a very common model, Intex's Glossy Panel Ball, has a stated diameter of 24 inches, that is, about 61 cm. Both smaller and much larger ones are on sale.

metro.name: Metre
metro.desc: The metre is the unit of length of the International System. Since 1983 it has been defined as the distance travelled by light in a vacuum in 1/299,792,458 of a second. In this way the speed of light is exactly 299,792,458 metres per second.

dodo.name: Dodo
dodo.desc: The dodo was a flightless bird that lived on the island of Mauritius, where Europeans encountered it at the end of the sixteenth century. It stood about a metre tall and weighed around 20 kg according to the Oxford University Museum of Natural History. The last confirmed sighting dates from 1662.

rafflesia.name: Rafflesia
rafflesia.desc: Rafflesia arnoldii is a parasitic plant with no leaves, stem or roots, which grows inside forest vines in Sumatra. Its flower is the largest single flower known: it exceeds a metre in diameter, with a record of 111 cm measured in 2020, and can weigh up to 11 kg. It gives off an unpleasant smell that attracts pollinating flies.

essere-umano.name: Human being
essere-umano.desc: The height of an adult human being varies greatly between populations and individuals. Among those born in 1996 the world average is 171 cm for men and 159 cm for women.

bicicletta.name: Bicycle
bicicletta.desc: A conventional adult bicycle is typically about 1.8 metres long and about 0.65 metres wide at the handlebars. These are the reference dimensions used in British guidelines for designing cycle routes. Cargo bikes and bicycles with trailers can be longer, so much so that a footprint of up to 2.8 metres is considered for designs.

verme-gigante-del-gippsland.name: Giant Gippsland earthworm
verme-gigante-del-gippsland.desc: The giant Gippsland earthworm (Megascolides australis) lives underground along stream banks in Gippsland, in the Australian state of Victoria. It is on average about a metre long and, stretched out, can exceed two metres; reports of three metres are not confirmed. The body has 300 to 400 segments and the animal can live ten years or more.

isetta.name: Isetta
isetta.desc: The Isetta is a microcar designed by Iso of Milan and built under licence by BMW from 1955. The BMW Isetta 250 Standard is 2,285 mm long, that is, about 2.3 m, and has a single-cylinder engine of 247 cm³. Of the first BMW version, more than 26,000 were sold.

girasole.name: Sunflower
girasole.desc: The common sunflower (Helianthus annuus) is an annual plant native to the western United States and Mexico. The stem is typically half a metre to 3 metres tall and bears flower heads 8 to 15 cm wide in the wild forms.

dal-pavimento-al-soffitto.name: Floor to ceiling
dal-pavimento-al-soffitto.desc: This is the minimum interior height required in Italy for living spaces: 2.70 m. Since 28 July 2024 the consolidated building code has allowed the designer to certify even lower rooms, down to the limit of 2.40 m, under certain conditions.

onde-radio-fm.name: FM radio waves
onde-radio-fm.desc: FM radio broadcasts in the band between 88 and 108 MHz. At these frequencies the wavelength goes from about 3.4 m to about 2.8 m: 3 m corresponds to 100 MHz, in the middle of the band.

albatro-urlatore.name: Wandering albatross
albatro-urlatore.desc: The wandering albatross (Diomedea exulans) is a large seabird of the southern oceans. Its wingspan ranges from 2.5 to 3.5 m, with an average of 3.1 m, and is considered the greatest among living birds. The body is 1.1 to 1.35 m long and weighs on average about 8 kg.

granchio-gigante-del-giappone.name: Japanese spider crab
granchio-gigante-del-giappone.desc: The Japanese spider crab (Macrocheira kaempferi) is the largest living arthropod known, though not the heaviest. With its legs outstretched an adult can approach 4 metres from claw to claw, while the carapace is only about 37 cm long. It lives on the seabed off Japan, on average between 150 and 300 metres deep.

automobile.name: Car
automobile.desc: An average car today is about 4.5 m long: a Volkswagen Golf, for example, measures 4.28 m. According to Transport & Environment, the average new car sold in Europe was 4.09 m long in 2000 and has been getting longer by about 1.2 cm a year since. If the trend continues, in 2040 it will reach 4.56 m.

giraffa.name: Giraffe
giraffa.desc: The giraffe (Giraffa camelopardalis) is the tallest mammal in the world and lives in the African savannas. Males reach about 5.7 m from the ground to the top of the horns, while females are 0.7–1 m shorter.

anaconda-verde.name: Green anaconda
anaconda-verde.desc: The green anaconda (Eunectes murinus) is a large semi-aquatic constrictor snake of South America. Females measure on average about 6 m and males about 3 m. Specimens of 9 m and more are reported, with masses up to 250 kg, but the real maximum size is much debated.

elefante-africano.name: African elephant
elefante-africano.desc: The African savanna elephant (Loxodonta africana) is the largest living land animal. The length of head and body, trunk included, ranges from 6 to 7.5 m; males stand 2.9 to 3.7 m tall at the shoulder and weigh on average about 6,000 kg.

modulo-lunare-apollo.name: Apollo Lunar Module
modulo-lunare-apollo.desc: The Apollo Lunar Module was the two-stage vehicle, built by Grumman, that carried two astronauts from lunar orbit to the surface of the Moon and back. With its legs extended it stood about 7 m tall and measured 9.4 m diagonally between the footpads of the landing gear. Between 1969 and 1972 six lunar modules took twelve astronauts to the Moon.

saguaro.name: Saguaro
saguaro.desc: The saguaro (Carnegiea gigantea) is the great columnar cactus of the Sonoran Desert. An adult specimen often exceeds 12 m and can reach about 15 m (50 feet), with a weight of 2 tonnes or more. It grows very slowly: the first arms normally appear between 60 and 75 years of age, and the average lifespan is estimated at 150–175 years.

autobus.name: Bus
autobus.desc: A standard two-axle city bus is about 12 m long. The Mercedes-Benz Citaro, for example, measures 12.14 m in length, 2.55 m in width and 3.12 m in height.

tyrannosaurus-rex.name: Tyrannosaurus rex
tyrannosaurus-rex.desc: Tyrannosaurus rex is a large carnivorous dinosaur that lived in North America at the end of the Cretaceous, between 68 and 66 million years ago. SUE, the skeleton at the Field Museum in Chicago, measures 40.5 feet (about 12.3 m) in length and is 4 m tall at the hip. It is the most complete T. rex skeleton by bone volume, about 90%, and was discovered in 1990 in South Dakota.

casa-media-negli-usa.name: Average US house
casa-media-negli-usa.desc: In the United States, single-family homes completed in 2025 have a median floor area of 2,142 square feet, about 199 m², according to the Census Bureau. On a single floor this equals a square about 14 m on a side, so the 15 m shown is an order of magnitude of the longer side and not a measured figure.

quercia.name: Oak
quercia.desc: The oak shown here is the English oak (Quercus robur), a large deciduous tree found across Europe. As an adult it is typically between 20 and 40 m tall. According to the Woodland Trust, oaks in the United Kingdom can host more than 2,300 different species.

schermo-solare-del-telescopio-webb.name: Webb telescope sunshield
schermo-solare-del-telescopio-webb.desc: The sunshield of the James Webb Space Telescope measures 21.2 m by 14.2 m, more or less the size of a tennis court. It is made of five layers of aluminium-coated Kapton: the first is 0.05 mm thick, the other four 0.025 mm. It keeps the telescope in the Sun's shadow so that it can observe in the infrared.

balenottera-azzurra.name: Blue whale
balenottera-azzurra.desc: The blue whale (Balaenoptera musculus) is the largest animal ever to have lived on Earth, according to NOAA. In the North Atlantic and North Pacific it reaches about 27 m, while in Antarctica it can reach about 33 m and exceed 150 tonnes.

maraapunisaurus.name: Maraapunisaurus
maraapunisaurus.desc: Maraapunisaurus fragillimus is a Jurassic sauropod described by Edward Cope in 1878 as Amphicoelias fragillimus and reclassified in 2018 as a basal rebbachisaurid. It is known from a single vertebra, now lost and documented only in the original publication. The 2018 revision estimates a vertebra 2.4 m tall and a total length between 30.3 and 32 m, much less than earlier estimates.

argentinosaurus.name: Argentinosaurus
argentinosaurus.desc: Argentinosaurus is a titanosaur sauropod that lived in Argentina in the Late Cretaceous, about 90 million years ago, and was described by Bonaparte and Coria in 1993. The Natural History Museum in London gives it a length of 35 m and a mass of 70,000 kg. It is among the largest dinosaurs known.

torre-di-pisa.name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
torre-di-pisa.desc: It is the bell tower of Pisa Cathedral, begun in 1174 and already leaning during construction. The Opera della Primaziale Pisana, which manages it, gives a height of 58.36 m, an outer diameter of 15 m and a weight of 14,453 tonnes. Inside, a staircase of 273 steps leads to the bell chamber with its seven bells.

boeing-747-8.name: Boeing 747-8
boeing-747-8.desc: The Boeing 747-8 is the latest version of the 747 and is 76.3 m long, 5.6 m more than the 747-400. The last one, a 747-8 freighter, was delivered to Atlas Air on 31 January 2023. In over half a century of production, the Everett factory built 1,574 Boeing 747s.

stazione-spaziale-internazionale.name: International Space Station
stazione-spaziale-internazionale.desc: The International Space Station measures 109 m from one end to the other, almost as much as an American football field. It has been continuously inhabited since November 2000. NASA has committed to using it until 2030, after which it will be brought down in a controlled re-entry.

campo-da-football-americano.name: American football field
campo-da-football-americano.desc: The NFL rules prescribe a rectangular field 360 feet long, that is, 109.7 m, and 160 feet wide, about 48.8 m. The length includes the two end zones, each 10 yards deep, on either side of the 100 yards of the playing field.

saturn-v.name: Saturn V
saturn-v.desc: The Saturn V is the rocket that took the astronauts of the Apollo missions to the Moon. It was 363 feet tall, that is, about 110.6 m, as tall as a 36-storey building, and at liftoff it produced a thrust of 34.5 million newtons. It flew from 1967 to 1973, when the last one put the Skylab station into orbit.

sequoia-hyperion.name: Hyperion redwood
sequoia-hyperion.desc: Hyperion is a coast redwood (Sequoia sempervirens) in Redwood National Park, California, and is the tallest living tree known. Discovered on 25 August 2006 by Chris Atkins and Michael Taylor, it measured 116.07 m in 2019. The exact location is kept secret and the area around the tree is closed to the public.

starship.name: Starship
starship.desc: Starship is the SpaceX rocket made up of the Super Heavy booster and the spacecraft of the same name. The V3 version, which flew for the first time on 22 May 2026, is about 124 m tall and produces a thrust of about 80 meganewtons at liftoff. It is the tallest and most powerful rocket ever built.

grande-piramide-di-giza.name: Great Pyramid of Giza
grande-piramide-di-giza.desc: It is the pyramid of the pharaoh Khufu at Giza, Egypt, the tallest in the world according to the Guinness World Records. Completed about 4,500 years ago, it was 146.7 m tall. Erosion and vandalism have lowered it to about 137–138 m.

dimorphos.name: Dimorphos
dimorphos.desc: Dimorphos is the small moon of the asteroid Didymos, with a diameter of about 151 m. On 26 September 2022 NASA's DART probe struck it on purpose, changing its orbit around Didymos. The European probe Hera, launched on 7 October 2024, is due to arrive in November 2026 to study the effects of the impact up close.

colosseo.name: Colosseum
colosseo.desc: The Flavian Amphitheatre in Rome, inaugurated by the emperor Titus in the year 80, is the largest amphitheatre in the world. The plan measures 189 m on the major axis and 156 m on the minor one, for an area of about 2 hectares. Estimates of its capacity vary greatly, from 45,000 to 87,000 spectators.

gateway-arch.name: Gateway Arch
gateway-arch.desc: It is the stainless-steel-clad arch that stands in St. Louis, Missouri, on the bank of the Mississippi. It is 630 feet tall, that is, 192 m, and just as wide between the outer faces of the two legs. It has the shape of an inverted catenary, and the National Park Service describes it as the tallest monument in the United States.

oumuamua.name: ʻOumuamua
oumuamua.desc: ʻOumuamua is the first interstellar object observed in the Solar System, discovered on 19 October 2017 by the Pan-STARRS1 telescope in Hawaii. It has never been resolved in an image: according to NASA it is up to 400 m long and perhaps ten times longer than wide, while Spitzer measurements limit the equivalent spherical diameter to a value between 100 and 440 m depending on the assumed composition. Its brightness varied by a factor of 10 every 7.3 hours.

diga-di-hoover.name: Hoover Dam
diga-di-hoover.desc: It is a concrete arch-gravity dam on the Colorado River, on the border between Arizona and Nevada. It measures 726.4 feet, that is, 221.4 m, from the foundation rock to the roadway on the crest. The body of the dam contains 3.25 million cubic yards of concrete, about 2.5 million m³, poured between June 1933 and May 1935.

titanic.name: Titanic
titanic.desc: The Titanic was an ocean liner 269 m long, with a gross tonnage of 46,329 tonnes. When launched it was the largest movable object ever put in the water. It sank on 15 April 1912 after striking an iceberg, and about 1,500 people died.

onde-radio-am.name: AM radio waves
onde-radio-am.desc: Medium-wave AM radio uses, according to the US standard, the band between 535 and 1,705 kHz. At these frequencies the wavelength goes from about 560 m to about 176 m: 300 m corresponds to 1 MHz.

torre-eiffel.name: Eiffel Tower
torre-eiffel.desc: The tower built by Gustave Eiffel for the Paris Universal Exposition of 1889 now reaches 330 m at the tip of the antennas. The architectural structure, without antennas, is 300 m tall and has a mass of about 8,000 tonnes.

apophis.name: Apophis
apophis.desc: Apophis is a near-Earth asteroid with a mean diameter of about 340 m, discovered on 19 June 2004. On 13 April 2029 it will pass about 32,000 km from the Earth's surface, closer than many satellites in geosynchronous orbit, with no risk of impact. NASA's OSIRIS-APEX probe has been redirected to study it during the flyby.

willis-tower.name: Willis Tower
willis-tower.desc: The Chicago skyscraper, called the Sears Tower until 2009, is 442.1 m tall to the roof and 527 m to the tip of the antennas. When it was completed, in 1973 according to the owner, it was the tallest building in the world.

international-commerce-centre.name: International Commerce Centre
international-commerce-centre.desc: The International Commerce Centre is an office and hotel skyscraper in Kowloon, Hong Kong, completed in 2010. It is 484 m tall and has 108 floors above ground. In the ranking of the Council on Vertical Urbanism it is the tallest building in Hong Kong and the thirteenth in the world.

bennu.name: Bennu
bennu.desc: Bennu is a carbon-rich near-Earth asteroid with a mean diameter of about 484 m and an equatorial diameter of about 500 m. NASA's OSIRIS-REx probe collected a sample from it on 20 October 2020 and delivered it to Earth on 24 September 2023. It rotates on its axis in 4.3 hours.

merdeka-118.name: Merdeka 118
merdeka-118.desc: Merdeka 118 is a 118-storey skyscraper in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, completed in 2023. Its architectural height, spire included, is 678.9 m, while the highest occupied floor is at 502.8 m. In the ranking of the Council on Vertical Urbanism it is the second tallest building in the world, after the Burj Khalifa.

burj-khalifa.name: Burj Khalifa
burj-khalifa.desc: The Burj Khalifa is a 163-storey skyscraper in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, inaugurated on 4 January 2010. With an architectural height of 828 m it is the tallest building in the world. The highest occupied floor is 584.5 m above the ground.

cascate-dell-angelo.name: Angel Falls
cascate-dell-angelo.desc: Salto Ángel, or Kerepakupai Merú, plunges from the Auyán tepui in Canaima National Park, Venezuela. The total drop is 979 m, with a single leap of 807 m, and it is recorded as the tallest waterfall in the world. The measurement dates from a 1949 expedition, and it is debated whether all 979 m belong to a single waterfall.

chilometro.name: Kilometre
chilometro.desc: The kilometre is a thousand metres: the SI prefix kilo stands for the factor 10³. One statute mile corresponds to 1.609344 kilometres.

fabbrica-boeing-di-everett.name: Boeing Everett Factory
fabbrica-boeing-di-everett.desc: The main Boeing assembly plant at Everett, Washington State, is recorded as the largest building in the world by volume: 13.4 million m³ on 39.8 hectares of covered area. It was built in the 1960s to produce the 747 and has grown a great deal since. Boeing does not publish the length of the building, so the value of about 1 km shown here is an estimate.

3i-atlas.name: 3I/ATLAS
3i-atlas.desc: 3I/ATLAS is a comet, the third known interstellar object, reported on 1 July 2025 by the ATLAS survey telescope in Chile. The nucleus is not directly visible: Hubble observations indicate a diameter between 440 m and 5.6 km, and a study based on non-gravitational acceleration puts it at around 1 km. It reached perihelion around 30 October 2025, at about 1.4 astronomical units from the Sun.

citta-del-vaticano.name: Vatican City
citta-del-vaticano.desc: Vatican City is an enclave within the city of Rome, created by the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929. Its territory measures at most 1,045 m in length and 850 m in width, for an area of 0.44 km². It is the smallest independent state in the world.

half-dome.name: Half Dome
half-dome.desc: Half Dome is a granodiorite dome in Yosemite National Park, California, smooth on three sides and with a vertical face on the fourth. The summit is at about 2,680 m above sea level and rises just under 1,500 m above the floor of Yosemite Valley. It was first climbed in 1875 by George Anderson and today is reached by a hike with 4,800 feet (about 1,460 m) of elevation gain.

miglio.name: Mile
miglio.desc: The statute mile is an Anglo-American unit of length equal to 1,609.344 metres, that is, 5,280 feet. In the United States there is also a mile based on the survey foot, longer by about 3 millimetres.

cruithne.name: Cruithne
cruithne.desc: Cruithne is a near-Earth asteroid with an effective diameter of about 2.07 km, measured in the infrared by the NEOWISE satellite. It makes one trip around the Sun in about a year, like the Earth, and seen from our planet it seems to follow a horseshoe orbit. It is not a moon of the Earth, but an orbital companion.

acceleratore-lineare-di-stanford.name: Stanford Linear Accelerator
acceleratore-lineare-di-stanford.desc: The linear accelerator of the SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, in California, is 2 miles long, that is, about 3.2 km, and produced its first particle beam on 21 May 1966. According to SLAC it is the longest linear accelerator ever built. Its beams led to the discovery of the charm quark and the tau lepton.

uluru.name: Uluru
uluru.desc: Uluru, formerly known as Ayers Rock, is a large sandstone monolith in the Northern Territory, Australia, about half a billion years old. It is about 3.6 km long, 348 m high above the plain and has a circumference of 9.4 km. For the Anangu, the traditional custodians, it is inseparable from Tjukurpa, the traditional law.

central-park.name: Central Park
