central-park.desc: Central Park is the large public park in the middle of Manhattan, New York, designed by Frederick Law Olmsted and Calvert Vaux and created in 1858. It extends from 59th to 110th Street for about 2.5 miles, that is, 4 km, and covers 843 acres, about 341 hectares. It receives about 42 million visits a year.

cometa-67p.name: Comet 67P
cometa-67p.desc: Comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko has a two-lobed nucleus measuring 4.34 × 2.60 × 2.12 km. The European probe Rosetta reached it in August 2014 and accompanied it along its orbit, and its lander Philae was the first to touch down on a comet. The mean density of the nucleus, 533 kg/m³, is about half that of water.

monte-bianco.name: Mont Blanc
monte-bianco.desc: Mont Blanc is the highest peak of the Alps and of Western Europe, on the border between Italy and France. The October 2026 measurement by the surveyors of Haute-Savoie gives 4,807.47 m, almost two metres more than in 2023. The elevation changes from one survey to another because wind and precipitation shift the snow that covers the summit.

palm-jebel-ali.name: Palm Jebel Ali
palm-jebel-ali.desc: Palm Jebel Ali is a large coastal project in Dubai, in the Jebel Ali area, developed by the company Nakheel. The plan approved in May 2023 gives an area of 13.4 km², twice that of Palm Jumeirah, and about 110 km of new coastline. The width of about 7 km used here is an indicative estimate: official sources do not report a length.

large-hadron-collider.name: Large Hadron Collider
large-hadron-collider.desc: CERN's Large Hadron Collider, near Geneva, is the largest and most powerful particle accelerator in the world. Its underground ring has a circumference of 26,659 m, which corresponds to a diameter of about 8.5 km, and contains 9,593 magnets. It started operating on 10 September 2008 in the tunnel originally built for LEP.

lep.name: LEP
lep.desc: CERN's LEP (Large Electron-Positron Collider) was the largest electron-positron accelerator ever built, with a circumference of 27 km and therefore a diameter of about 8.5 km. It entered service in July 1989 and was shut down on 2 November 2000. Its tunnel now houses the Large Hadron Collider.

monte-everest.name: Mount Everest
monte-everest.desc: Everest, on the border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China, is the highest mountain on Earth above sea level. Its summit is at 8,848.86 m, according to the measurement announced in 2020 by Chinese and Nepalese surveyors. The first documented ascent was by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay, on 29 May 1953.

fossa-delle-marianne-profondita.name: Mariana Trench (depth)
fossa-delle-marianne-profondita.desc: Challenger Deep, in the Mariana Trench, is the deepest point of the seas: it lies in the Pacific Ocean, about 300 km south-west of Guam. The crewed dives of June 2020 measured 10,935 m, with an uncertainty of 6 m. Measurements made from the surface give different values, from 10,900 to 11,034 m.

deimos.name: Deimos
deimos.desc: Deimos is the smaller of the two moons of Mars, discovered on 11 August 1877 by Asaph Hall. It is irregular in shape: the longest axis measures about 15.6 km, against a mean diameter of about 12.4 km. It orbits Mars about every 30 hours.

cometa-di-halley.name: Halley's Comet
cometa-di-halley.desc: Halley's Comet has a nucleus of about 15 × 8 km, photographed up close in 1986 by the European probe Giotto. It is among the darkest objects in the Solar System: it reflects only 3% of the light it receives. It travels its orbit on average in 76 years and will be visible again in 2061.

olympus-mons-altezza.name: Olympus Mons (height)
olympus-mons-altezza.desc: Olympus Mons is a shield volcano on Mars, the largest volcano and the tallest mountain in the Solar System. The Guinness World Records gives 25 km from base to summit, almost three times Everest, but the value changes depending on the reference chosen to measure it. Despite its height it has very gentle slopes, because it is over 20 times wider than it is tall.

fobos.name: Phobos
fobos.desc: Phobos is the larger of the two moons of Mars, irregular in shape: the longest axis measures about 26 km, against a mean diameter of about 22 km. It orbits so close to the planet that it completes three orbits a day. The Japanese MMX mission, launched on 20 October 2026, aims to bring samples back to Earth in 2031.

stella-di-neutroni.name: Neutron star
stella-di-neutroni.desc: A neutron star is the compact remnant of the core of a massive star that exploded as a supernova. Measurements by the NICER X-ray telescope give a radius of about 12.7 km for the pulsar PSR J0030+0451 (1.34 solar masses) and about 12.4 km for PSR J0740+6620 (2.07 solar masses), with uncertainties of about 1 km. More mass than the Sun therefore fits in a sphere about 24 km across.

future-circular-collider.name: Future Circular Collider
future-circular-collider.desc: The Future Circular Collider is the accelerator proposed by CERN as the successor to the LHC: a ring 90.7 km in circumference, that is, about 29 km in diameter, in a tunnel at an average depth of 200 m under France and Switzerland. The feasibility study was published in 2025. It is not yet approved: the decision on construction is expected around 2028.

ganymed.name: Ganymed
ganymed.desc: (1036) Ganymed is an Amor-type asteroid discovered in 1924 by Walter Baade and is considered the largest near-Earth asteroid. Diameter estimates range from about 35 to about 40 km depending on the measurement method. It is not to be confused with Ganymede, the moon of Jupiter, and its orbit does not cross that of the Earth: the perihelion is at 1.24 astronomical units from the Sun.

arrokoth.name: Arrokoth
arrokoth.desc: Arrokoth, formerly known as 2014 MU69, is a small Kuiper belt object made of two lobes in contact and about 35 km long. The New Horizons probe flew past it on 1 January 2019: it is the most distant object ever explored up close by a probe. It was discovered in 2014 with the Hubble Space Telescope and is even redder than Pluto.

maratona.name: Marathon
maratona.desc: The marathon is the longest running race in the Olympic programme: 42.195 km, equal to 26 miles and 385 yards. The distance dates from the 1908 London Games, when the course was lengthened so that it could start from Windsor Castle. It was fixed as the standard in 1921.

nix.name: Nix
nix.desc: Nix is a small moon of Pluto, discovered in 2005 with the Hubble Space Telescope. New Horizons images from 2015 show an elongated body of about 50 × 35 × 33 km. Its surface is highly reflective, with a geometric albedo of about 0.56, and it rotates in about 1.8 days without always showing the same face to Pluto.

idra.name: Hydra
idra.desc: Hydra is the outermost of the two moons of Pluto discovered in 2005 with the Hubble Space Telescope. It is an elongated body of about 62 × 37 × 29 km, measured thanks to the New Horizons flyby in 2015. It rotates on its axis in about 10 hours, much faster than the 38 days it takes to complete an orbit, and has a bright surface with an albedo of about 0.83.

bianca.name: Bianca
bianca.desc: Bianca is one of the small inner moons of Uranus, with a diameter of about 51–54 km. It was discovered on 23 January 1986 in images from the Voyager 2 probe, together with nine other satellites of the planet. It is a dark body, reflecting only about 7% of the light it receives.

buco-nero-stellare.name: Stellar black hole
buco-nero-stellare.desc: A stellar-mass black hole is born from the collapse of the core of a very massive star. The example shown here has 10 solar masses: the Schwarzschild radius is about 2.95 km per solar mass, so the event horizon has a diameter of about 59 km. According to NASA, the masses of these objects range from a few to hundreds of times that of the Sun.

rhode-island.name: Rhode Island
rhode-island.desc: Rhode Island is the smallest of the United States: it is about 48 miles long, that is, 77 km, and 37 miles wide, about 60 km. It lies in the north-east of the country, between Massachusetts, Connecticut and the Atlantic Ocean, with Providence as its capital. It is one of the 13 original states.

belinda.name: Belinda
belinda.desc: Belinda is a small inner moon of Uranus, with a mean diameter of about 90 km. It was discovered on 13 January 1986 in images from the Voyager 2 probe and is one of the ten satellites of Uranus found by the mission. Its surface is dark and reflects about 7% of the light.

brunei.name: Brunei
brunei.desc: Brunei is a small sultanate on the north-western coast of the island of Borneo, with Bandar Seri Begawan as its capital and an area of 5,765 km². It is surrounded by the Malaysian state of Sarawak, which divides it into two parts with a strip of territory. The extent of about 120 km used here is an indicative estimate, not an official measurement.

galatea.name: Galatea
galatea.desc: Galatea is a small inner moon of Neptune of irregular shape: the longest axis measures about 204 km, against a mean diameter of about 176 km. It was discovered in July 1989 by the science team of the Voyager 2 probe. Its gravity is thought to disturb the rings of Neptune.

gaia-bh3.name: Gaia BH3
gaia-bh3.desc: Gaia BH3 is a dormant black hole in a binary system about 1900 light-years from Earth, identified in the astrometric data of the Gaia satellite and announced in 2024. Its mass, derived from the orbit of the companion star, is 32.7 solar masses. At the time of its discovery it was the most massive black hole of stellar origin known in the Milky Way.

psyche.name: Psyche
psyche.desc: (16) Psyche is a large metal-rich asteroid of the main belt, with an irregular potato-like shape. At its widest point it measures about 278 km, against an equivalent diameter of about 222 km. NASA's Psyche probe, launched on 13 October 2023, is due to begin its mission around the asteroid in August 2029.

ruanda.name: Rwanda
ruanda.desc: Rwanda is a small landlocked country in east-central Africa, with an area of 26,338 km². At its point of greatest extent, from north-east to south-west, it measures about 248 km, while in the perpendicular direction it reaches 166 km. It is called "the land of a thousand hills" and its territory rises from 950 to 4,500 metres above sea level.

nereide.name: Nereid
nereide.desc: Nereid is one of the outermost moons of Neptune, discovered by Gerard Kuiper on 1 May 1949. Its diameter is estimated at about 357 km from thermal measurements by the Spitzer and Herschel telescopes, close to the 340 km derived from the Voyager 2 probe. Its orbit is among the most eccentric of the moons in the Solar System, with an eccentricity of 0.75, and takes 360 days to complete.

mimas.name: Mimas
mimas.desc: Mimas is the smallest and innermost of the major moons of Saturn, with a mean diameter of about 396 km. The crater Herschel, 130 km wide, covers a third of its diameter. A study published in Nature in 2024, based on data from the Cassini probe, indicates that beneath the icy crust lies a global ocean formed less than 25 million years ago.

west-virginia.name: West Virginia
west-virginia.desc: West Virginia is a US state in the Appalachian Mountains region, with Charleston as its capital and an area of about 62,760 km². From east to west it extends for 265 miles, that is, about 426 km, and from north to south for a maximum of 381 km. It has one of the most irregular shapes among the American states, with two narrow strips of territory to the north and east.

grand-canyon.name: Grand Canyon
grand-canyon.desc: The Grand Canyon is the gorge carved by the Colorado River in the Arizona plateau. Measured along the river, from Lees Ferry to the Grand Wash Cliffs, it is 277 miles long, that is, 446 km. On average it is 16 km wide from one rim to the other and about 1.6 km deep.

miranda.name: Miranda
miranda.desc: Miranda is the smallest of the five major moons of Uranus, with a mean diameter of about 472 km, and was discovered by Gerard Kuiper in 1948. The Voyager 2 probe in 1986 revealed a very varied surface, marked by large fault canyons. The escarpment Verona Rupes, the tallest known in the Solar System, is estimated to be about 20 km deep.

encelado.name: Enceladus
encelado.desc: Enceladus is an icy moon of Saturn with a mean diameter of about 504 km. From the south pole, geyser-like jets throw water vapour and ice grains from an underground ocean into space. In data from the Cassini probe, complex organic molecules were found and, in 2023, phosphates.

vesta.name: Vesta
vesta.desc: Vesta is the second most massive body in the main asteroid belt, after Ceres: it measures about 569 × 555 × 453 km, with a mean diameter of about 525 km. NASA's Dawn probe orbited it from 16 July 2011 to 5 September 2012. The crater Rheasilvia, about 500 km wide, is almost as large as the asteroid itself.

dysnomia.name: Dysnomia
dysnomia.desc: Dysnomia is the only known moon of the dwarf planet Eris. Its diameter is not measured directly: a thermal model based on data from the ALMA radio telescope gives 615 km, with a range from 565 to 675 km, while the previous estimate by the same authors was 700 ± 115 km. The surface is very dark, with an albedo of about 0.05.

cerere.name: Ceres
cerere.desc: Ceres is the largest body in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter and the only dwarf planet in the inner Solar System, with a mean diameter of about 939 km. It was discovered by Giuseppe Piazzi in 1801. In 2015 NASA's Dawn probe reached it, making it the first dwarf planet visited by a spacecraft.

megametro.name: Megametre
megametro.desc: The megametre is a million metres, that is, a thousand kilometres: the SI prefix mega stands for the factor 10⁶. The Earth's equatorial diameter, 12,756 kilometres, corresponds to about 12.8 megametres.

sedna.name: Sedna
sedna.desc: Sedna is a trans-Neptunian object with a very elongated orbit, which even at its closest point to the Sun stays at about 76 astronomical units. It has never been resolved in an image: thermal measurements by the Herschel Space Telescope give a diameter of 995 ± 80 km, so between about 915 and 1,075 km. When discovered, in 2003, it was the most distant object ever observed in the Solar System.

quaoar.name: Quaoar
quaoar.desc: Quaoar is a dwarf planet beyond the orbit of Neptune, at almost 44 times the Earth–Sun distance, with an estimated radius of 555 km, that is, a diameter of about 1,110 km. In 2023 a dense ring was announced at almost seven and a half times the radius of Quaoar, far beyond the Roche limit. According to classical theory, at that distance the material should have gathered into a small moon.

italia.name: Italy
italia.desc: Italy is a boot-shaped peninsula that stretches into the Mediterranean for about 1,185 km from north-west to south-east, with a maximum width of 381 km. Including Sicily and Sardinia, its area is about 301,000 km². Between the Vetta d'Italia, in the Alps, and the southern coast of Lampedusa there are about 11 and a half degrees of latitude, equal to almost 1,290 km.

caronte.name: Charon
caronte.desc: Charon is the largest of the five moons of Pluto, with a diameter of about 1,212 km. It is about half the size of Pluto: no other known satellite is so large relative to its planet. The two bodies always show each other the same face, and Charon completes an orbit in 6.4 Earth days.

gonggong.name: Gonggong
gonggong.desc: Gonggong, formerly known as 2007 OR10, is a large trans-Neptunian object discovered at Palomar on 17 July 2007. Thermal measurements combined with the orbit of its moon Xiangliu give a diameter of 1,230 ± 50 km. With a mass of 1.75 × 10²¹ kg it is the fifth dwarf planet by mass after Eris, Pluto, Haumea and Makemake.

california.name: California
california.desc: California is a US state facing the Pacific Ocean, between Oregon to the north and Mexico to the south, with Sacramento as its capital. Its maximum north–south extent is about 780 miles, that is, around 1,250 km, while from east to west it measures about 560 km. It is the third largest American state by area and the first by population.

texas.name: Texas
texas.desc: Texas is a southern US state, the largest of the federation after Alaska, with Austin as its capital. The maximum straight-line distance is 801 miles, about 1,290 km, from the north-west corner of the Panhandle to the Rio Grande below Brownsville. From east to west, between the Sabine River and the area around El Paso, it measures 773 miles, about 1,244 km.

makemake.name: Makemake
makemake.desc: Makemake is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt with a diameter of about 1,430 km. A stellar occultation observed in 2011 showed a slightly flattened shape, with axes of 1,430 ± 9 km and 1,502 ± 45 km, and no global atmosphere like that of Pluto. Seen from Earth it is the second brightest object in the Kuiper belt after Pluto.

haumea.name: Haumea
haumea.desc: Haumea is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt of very elongated shape: the major axis measures at least 2,322 km, while the sphere of equal volume has a diameter of about 1,595 km. It rotates on its axis in 3.9 hours, one of the fastest rotations among the large bodies of the Solar System. In 2017 a stellar occultation revealed a ring 70 km wide with a radius of about 2,287 km.

titania.name: Titania
titania.desc: Titania is the largest moon of Uranus, with a mean diameter of about 1,578 km. The Voyager 2 probe photographed on it a system of fault valleys up to about 1,600 km long, a sign of ancient geological activity.

grande-barriera-corallina.name: Great Barrier Reef
grande-barriera-corallina.desc: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef system in the world and lies in the Coral Sea, off Queensland, Australia. It extends for 1,429 miles, that is, about 2,300 km, and is made up of almost 3,000 distinct reefs. Much of its area is protected by a marine park managed by an Australian authority.

eris.name: Eris
eris.desc: Eris is a dwarf planet beyond the orbit of Neptune. The occultation of a star observed in 2010 gave a diameter of 2,326 km, with an uncertainty of 12 km: about 50 km less than Pluto. Its mass, however, is 27% greater than that of Pluto.

plutone.name: Pluto
plutone.desc: Pluto is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, with a diameter of about 2,377 km, equal to about two thirds of that of the Moon. The only probe that has visited it up close is NASA's New Horizons, which flew past it on 14 July 2015.

tritone.name: Triton
tritone.desc: Triton is the largest moon of Neptune, with a mean diameter of about 2,705 km. It is the only large moon in the Solar System with a retrograde orbit, that is, one travelled in the direction opposite to the planet's rotation. Its crust is made of frozen nitrogen.

europa.name: Europa
europa.desc: Europa is one of the four Galilean moons of Jupiter, with a mean diameter of about 3,122 km, a little less than that of the Moon. NASA's Europa Clipper probe, which left on 14 October 2024, will reach Jupiter in April 2030 and make 49 close flybys of Europa.

luna.name: Moon
luna.desc: The Moon is the Earth's only natural satellite, with a mean diameter of about 3,475 km. The Artemis II mission, which left on 1 April 2026 and returned on 10 April, took four astronauts around the Moon: for NASA it is the first crewed lunar flyby in 50 years.

io.name: Io
io.desc: Io is the innermost of the four Galilean moons of Jupiter, with a mean diameter of about 3,643 km, a little more than the Moon. It is the body with the greatest volcanic activity in the Solar System: it has hundreds of volcanoes, powered by the tides caused by Jupiter and the nearby moons.

larghezza-degli-stati-uniti.name: Width of the United States
larghezza-degli-stati-uniti.desc: This is the coast-to-coast distance across the 48 contiguous US states. According to the US Geological Survey, from West Quoddy Head in Maine to the Pacific, along the parallel, there are 2,742 miles, about 4,413 km. The two points farthest from each other, West Quoddy Head and Point Arena in California, are 2,892 miles apart, about 4,654 km.

callisto.name: Callisto
callisto.desc: Callisto is the second largest moon of Jupiter and the third in the Solar System, with a mean diameter of about 4,821 km. According to NASA it is the most heavily cratered object in the Solar System. Data from the Galileo probe indicate that it might hide a salty ocean beneath the surface.

mercurio.name: Mercury
mercurio.desc: Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun, with a mean diameter of about 4,879 km. The ESA and JAXA probe BepiColombo, which left on 20 October 2018, was designed to study it from orbit. ESA's mission plan sets orbit insertion for 21 November 2026 and the start of scientific observations for April 2027.

titano.name: Titan
titano.desc: Titan is the largest moon of Saturn, with a mean diameter of about 5,150 km. It is the only moon in the Solar System with a dense atmosphere and the only place beyond Earth with stable liquids on the surface, in the form of hydrocarbon lakes and seas. The launch of NASA's Dragonfly drone is planned for no earlier than July 2028, with arrival at the end of 2034.

ganimede.name: Ganymede
ganimede.desc: Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter, is the largest in the Solar System: with a mean diameter of about 5,262 km it is even bigger than the planet Mercury. It is the only moon with a magnetic field of its own. ESA's Juice probe, which left on 14 April 2023, will arrive at Jupiter in July 2031 and end its mission in orbit around Ganymede.

marte.name: Mars
marte.desc: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun, a rocky world with a mean diameter of about 6,779 km, a little more than half that of the Earth, and two small moons, Phobos and Deimos. Its day lasts 24.66 hours, almost as long as ours, and the pressure at the surface is just 6.36 millibars.

asia.name: Asia
asia.desc: Asia is the largest of the continents, with an area of about 44.6 million km² including inland waters. The mainland extends over more than 75 degrees of latitude, from Cape Chelyuskin in Siberia to Cape Piai on the Malay Peninsula, that is, about 8,500 km from north to south. It is home to the highest mountains on Earth, including Everest.

trappist-1-e.name: TRAPPIST-1 e
trappist-1-e.desc: TRAPPIST-1 e is a rocky exoplanet about 40 light-years from Earth, with a radius 0.92 times that of the Earth, that is, a diameter of about 11,700 km. It orbits a red dwarf in 6.1 days, at a distance at which liquid water on the surface is theoretically possible if the planet has an atmosphere. The Webb telescope is observing it: the first four transits indicate that it does not retain a primary atmosphere of hydrogen and helium, while the possibility of a secondary atmosphere remains open.

sirio-b.name: Sirius B
sirio-b.desc: Sirius B is the nearest and brightest white dwarf in the sky, the companion of Sirius A, around which it orbits in 50.13 years. It has a mass of 1.018 solar masses and a radius of about 0.0081 solar radii, that is, a diameter of 11,300–11,700 km, a little less than that of the Earth. A mass equal to that of the Sun is therefore squeezed into a volume smaller than that of our planet.

venere.name: Venus
venere.desc: Venus is the second planet from the Sun and has a mean diameter of about 12,104 km, 95% of that of the Earth. Its dense atmosphere produces a pressure of 92 bar at the surface and a mean temperature of 464 °C. It rotates in a retrograde direction and very slowly: a solar day lasts about 117 Earth days.

terra.name: Earth
terra.desc: The Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the largest of the four rocky planets, with a mean diameter of about 12,742 km. It is not a perfect sphere: the equatorial radius measures 6,378.1 km and the polar one 6,356.8 km, a difference of about 21 km. It has a mean temperature of 15 °C and a single natural satellite, the Moon.

grande-muraglia-cinese.name: Great Wall of China
grande-muraglia-cinese.desc: The Great Wall is a set of fortifications built in China by different dynasties over more than 2,000 years. In June 2012 the State Administration of Cultural Heritage set its official length, branches included, at 21,196.18 km. The previous estimate of 8,851.8 km concerned only the walls of the Ming dynasty.

k2-18-b.name: K2-18 b
k2-18-b.desc: K2-18 b is a sub-Neptune planet 120 light-years from Earth, with a mass 8.6 times that of the Earth and an estimated radius between 2.37 and 2.6 Earth radii, that is, a diameter between about 30,000 and 33,000 km. In 2023 the Webb telescope detected methane and carbon dioxide in its atmosphere. The possible dimethyl sulfide signal, proposed as a biosignature in 2025, is not confirmed: a joint analysis of all the Webb data found insufficient statistical evidence.

nettuno.name: Neptune
nettuno.desc: Neptune is the eighth planet of the Solar System and the farthest from the Sun, a giant with a mean diameter of about 49,244 km at the 1 bar pressure level, almost four times that of the Earth. It takes about 165 years to complete an orbit and has 16 known moons. In its atmosphere, winds of up to 580 m/s, over 2,000 km/h, have been measured.

urano.name: Uranus
urano.desc: Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun, a giant with a mean diameter of about 50,724 km at the 1 bar pressure level, four times that of the Earth. Its rotation axis is tilted by 97.77° relative to its orbit, so the planet rotates almost lying on its side. It takes 84 years to complete an orbit and has 28 known moons.

mondo-di-minecraft.name: Minecraft world
mondo-di-minecraft.desc: In Minecraft Java Edition the playable world is a square bounded by the world border, at most 59,999,968 blocks wide, that is, about 60 million. Each block equals one metre, so the world measures about 60,000 km on a side. The limit is a software choice and applies only to this edition of the game.

orbita-geostazionaria.name: Geostationary orbit
orbita-geostazionaria.desc: A satellite 42,164 km from the centre of the Earth, that is, at an altitude of about 36,000 km, takes 23 hours, 56 minutes and 4 seconds to complete an orbit: exactly one rotation of the Earth. The diameter of the orbit is therefore about 84,300 km. Seen from the ground, a geostationary satellite above the equator stays fixed at the same point in the sky, which is useful for meteorology and telecommunications.

saturno.name: Saturn
saturno.desc: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and the second largest, with a mean diameter of about 116,460 km at the 1 bar pressure level, rings excluded. It is strongly flattened at the poles: the equatorial diameter is 120,536 km, the polar one 108,728 km. Its mean density, 687 kg/m³, is lower than that of water, and NASA's fact sheet credits it with 274 moons.

eblm-j0555-57ab.name: EBLM J0555-57Ab
eblm-j0555-57ab.desc: EBLM J0555-57Ab is a small star that eclipses a Sun-like companion every 7.8 days, described in 2017. It has a mass of about 85 times that of Jupiter (0.081 solar masses) and a radius of 0.084 solar radii, so a diameter of about 117,000 km, comparable to that of Saturn. Its mass is close to the minimum limit for hydrogen fusion.

gliese-229-b.name: Gliese 229 B
gliese-229-b.desc: Gliese 229 B, discovered in 1995 around a red dwarf at 5.76 parsecs, is the first known T-type brown dwarf. In 2024 it was found to be a pair, Gliese 229 Ba and Bb, of 38.1 and 34.4 Jupiter masses, which orbit each other every 12.1 days at 0.042 astronomical units. The radii of the two components have not been measured: estimates made when it was thought to be a single object range from about 0.94 to 1.1 Jupiter radii.

giove.name: Jupiter
giove.desc: Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun and the largest in the Solar System, with a mean diameter of about 139,820 km at the 1 bar pressure level, almost eleven times that of the Earth. Its mass is 318 times that of the Earth. It rotates very fast, with a day of just 9.93 hours, and has 95 known moons.

trappist-1.name: TRAPPIST-1
trappist-1.desc: TRAPPIST-1 is an ultracool red dwarf around which seven known planets orbit. Its radius is 0.1192 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 166,000 km, a little more than that of Jupiter. The densities of all seven planets are consistent with a rocky composition.

wolf-359.name: Wolf 359
wolf-359.desc: Wolf 359 is an M6-type red dwarf about 7.9 light-years away, among the stars closest to the Sun. It has a radius of 0.144 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 200,000 km, and a mass of 0.110 solar masses. The surface temperature is about 2,750 kelvin, less than half that of the Sun.

proxima-centauri.name: Proxima Centauri
proxima-centauri.desc: Proxima Centauri is the star closest to the Sun, about 4.2 light-years away, and is gravitationally bound to the pair Alpha Centauri A and B with an orbit of about 550,000 years. The adopted radius is 0.154 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 215,000 km, while the direct interferometric measurement gives 0.141 solar radii (about 196,000 km). Its mass is about 12% of that of the Sun.

tres-4-b.name: TrES-4 b
tres-4-b.desc: TrES-4 b is a hot Jupiter discovered in 2007, which orbits its star in 3.55 days. It has a mass lower than that of Jupiter but an estimated radius between 1.61 and 1.78 Jupiter radii according to different analyses, that is, a diameter between about 230,000 and 255,000 km. At the time of discovery it was the transiting planet with the largest radius and lowest density known.

anelli-di-saturno.name: Saturn's rings
anelli-di-saturno.desc: The main rings of Saturn (C, B and A) extend up to 136,780 km from the centre of the planet, for a diameter of about 273,600 km. Counting also the thin F ring, at 139,826 km, it comes to about 280,000 km. The typical thickness of the main rings, on the other hand, is only about 10 metres.

distanza-terra-luna.name: Earth–Moon distance
distanza-terra-luna.desc: The Moon orbits at a mean distance of 384,400 km from the Earth, measured between the centres of the two bodies. The orbit is elliptical: the distance varies from about 363,300 km at perigee to 405,500 km at apogee. Laser measurements on the reflectors left by the Apollo missions show that the Moon is moving away by 3.8 cm a year.

stella-di-kapteyn.name: Kapteyn's Star
stella-di-kapteyn.desc: Kapteyn's Star is a metal-poor red dwarf at 3.91 parsecs (about 12.8 light-years) and is the Galactic halo star closest to the Sun. Its measured radius is 0.291 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 405,000 km. From its halo-star kinematics and low metallicity it is assigned an age of more than 10 billion years.

stella-di-luyten.name: Luyten's Star
stella-di-luyten.desc: Luyten's Star (GJ 273) is an M3.5-type red dwarf about 12.4 light-years from the Sun. It has a radius of 0.319 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 444,000 km, and a mass of about 0.30 solar masses. Its surface temperature is about 3,300 kelvin.

gliese-229-a.name: Gliese 229 A
gliese-229-a.desc: Gliese 229 A is an M1-type red dwarf at 5.76 parsecs (about 18.8 light-years) from the Sun, with a mass of 0.579 solar masses. Its radius is estimated at 0.53 ± 0.05 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 740,000 km with a margin of about 70,000 km. Gliese 229 B, the first T-type brown dwarf discovered, orbits it.

gigametro.name: Gigametre
gigametro.desc: The gigametre is a billion metres, that is, a million kilometres: the SI prefix giga stands for the factor 10⁹. The diameter of the Sun is about 1.4 gigametres. The mean distance between the Earth and the Sun is about 150 gigametres.

alfa-centauri-b.name: Alpha Centauri B
alfa-centauri-b.desc: Alpha Centauri B is a K1-type orange star, the smaller component of the Alpha Centauri pair, the nearest Sun-like system to us. VLTI interferometric measurements give an angular diameter of 5.999 milliarcseconds and a radius of 0.8632 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 1.2 million km. Its companion Alpha Centauri A is larger, at 1.2234 solar radii.

sole.name: Sun
sole.desc: The Sun is the star of the Solar System. The nominal solar radius set by the International Astronomical Union in 2015 is 695,700 km, so the diameter is 1,391,400 km. It is an exact conventional value, used as a unit for other stars, based on a measurement of the photospheric radius of 695,658 ± 140 km.

distanza-del-telescopio-webb.name: Distance of the Webb telescope
distanza-del-telescopio-webb.desc: The James Webb Space Telescope does not orbit the Earth but the Sun, 1.5 million km from our planet, near the second Lagrange point (L2). From there it stays aligned with the Earth as the Earth goes around the Sun, so the large sunshield can protect the telescope from the light and heat of the Sun, Earth and Moon. It took about 30 days to reach that position.

alfa-centauri-a.name: Alpha Centauri A
alfa-centauri-a.desc: Alpha Centauri A is the main star of the triple system closest to the Sun, about 4 light-years away. Its radius, measured with the VLTI interferometer, is 1.2234 times that of the Sun, equal to a diameter of about 1.7 million km. In 2025 the Webb telescope observed a gas giant planet candidate there, not yet confirmed.

sirio-a.name: Sirius A
sirio-a.desc: Sirius A is the brightest star in the night sky, in the constellation Canis Major. Its diameter, measured with the VLTI interferometer, is 1.711 times that of the Sun, that is, about 2.38 million km. Sirius B, a white dwarf smaller than the Earth but with 98% of the Sun's mass, orbits it.

altair.name: Altair
altair.desc: Altair is the brightest star in Aquila and rotates so fast that it is flattened at the poles. The CHARA interferometer imaged its surface: the radius is 1.634 solar radii at the poles and 2.029 at the equator, that is, diameters of about 2.27 and 2.82 million km. The value shown, 2.5 million km, is a middle figure between the two.

procione.name: Procyon
procione.desc: Procyon A is an F5-type star in Canis Minor, among those closest to the Sun. Its diameter, measured with the VLTI interferometer, is 2.048 times that of the Sun, that is, about 2.85 million km. According to models it is ending its main-sequence phase, at an age of about 2.3 billion years.

vega.name: Vega
vega.desc: Vega, in Lyra, is an A0-type star long used as a reference for measuring the brightness of other stars. It rotates rapidly and we see it almost pole-on: the radius is 2.418 solar radii at the poles and 2.726 at the equator, for a mean diameter of about 3.6 million km. Its age is estimated at around 700 million years.

regolo.name: Regulus
regolo.desc: Regulus is the main star of Leo, of type B7. It rotates at 96% of its critical velocity, so much so that the equatorial radius (4.21 solar radii) exceeds the polar one (3.22) by about 30%: the diameter ranges from 4.5 to 5.9 million km, with an average of about 5.2. The poles are over 3000 K hotter than the equator.

perielio-della-parker-solar-probe.name: Parker Solar Probe perihelion
perielio-della-parker-solar-probe.desc: On 24 December 2024 NASA's Parker Solar Probe passed 3.8 million miles, about 6.1 million km, from the surface of the Sun: almost 6.9 million km from its centre. At that moment it was travelling at about 692,000 km/h, that is, 192 km/s. According to NASA it is the highest speed ever reached by a human-made object.

spica.name: Spica
spica.desc: Spica, in Virgo, is a close binary system of two hot, massive stars. The primary has a radius of 7.47 ± 0.54 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 10.4 million km, and a mass of about 11.4 solar masses. It is a pulsating variable of the Beta Cephei type and the system has an estimated age of 12.5 million years.

pollux.name: Pollux
pollux.desc: Pollux, in Gemini, is a K-type orange giant around which a planet orbits. The angular diameter measured by interferometry, 7.96 milliarcseconds, corresponds to a radius of 8.8 ± 0.1 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 12 million km. From its oscillations a mass of 1.91 solar masses is derived.

altezza-totale-dell-umanita.name: Combined height of humanity
altezza-totale-dell-umanita.desc: If all human beings stood on top of one another, they would form a column of about 13 million km, more than 30 times the distance between the Earth and the Moon. It is an estimate: the UN counted 8.2 billion people in 2024 and adults are on average 171 cm (men) and 159 cm (women) tall, but children are counted too. With an average height between 1.5 and 1.65 m the total ranges from about 12 to 14 million km.

capella.name: Capella
capella.desc: Capella, in Auriga, appears as a single star but is a binary system of two giants of almost equal mass, about 2.5 times that of the Sun. The primary has a radius of 11.98 ± 0.57 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 16.7 million km, while the secondary measures 8.83 solar radii. The primary is at the end of the phase in which it burns helium in its core.

sistema-di-trappist-1.name: TRAPPIST-1 system
sistema-di-trappist-1.desc: TRAPPIST-1 is an M-type star around which Earth-like planets orbit. The outermost, TRAPPIST-1 h, announced in 2017, is 0.06189 astronomical units from the star and completes an orbit in 18.8 days: the diameter of its orbit is about 18.5 million km. The whole system would fit inside the orbit of Mercury six times over.

vv-cephei-b.name: VV Cephei B
vv-cephei-b.desc: VV Cephei B is the blue companion, of type B0–B2, of the red supergiant VV Cephei A, which eclipses it about every 20 years. Its radius is estimated between 13 and 25 solar radii, that is, a diameter between about 18 and 35 million km: the value shown, 25 million km, lies within this range. The star is surrounded by a disc of gas captured from the wind of its companion, which makes it hard to measure.

sagittarius-a.name: Sagittarius A*
sagittarius-a.desc: Sagittarius A* is the supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way. Its mass, measured in 2021 by the GRAVITY collaboration by following the orbits of nearby stars, is 4.3 million solar masses. The first image was published in 2022 by the Event Horizon Telescope.

alnitak.name: Alnitak
alnitak.desc: Alnitak (Zeta Orionis) is one of the three stars of Orion's Belt and is a triple system. The main component is a blue supergiant of type O9.5 with a radius of 20 ± 3 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 28 million km, with a range between 23 and 32. The value depends on the adopted distance, 387 parsecs, while the orbit of the system would indicate 294.

arturo.name: Arcturus
arturo.desc: Arcturus, in Boötes, is a red giant with a mass of about 1.08 solar masses, a little more than the Sun. Its radius is 25.4 ± 0.2 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 35.3 million km. It has an estimated age of 7.1 billion years and a chemical composition typical of the stars of the Galaxy's thick disc.

distanza-mercurio-sole.name: Mercury–Sun distance
distanza-mercurio-sole.desc: Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun: it orbits it at a mean distance of 57.9 million km, that is, 0.387 times that of the Earth. The orbit is very elongated, so much so that the distance varies from 46.0 million km at perihelion to 69.8 million at aphelion. A full orbit lasts 88 days.

r136a1.name: R136a1
r136a1.desc: R136a1 is a Wolf-Rayet star in the cluster R136, in the Large Magellanic Cloud. Analysis of Hubble spectra assigns it a radius of about 42.7 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 59 million km. It is the most massive star known: estimates range from 170 to 230 solar masses according to the 2022 Gemini observations, up to over 250 according to other studies.

aldebaran.name: Aldebaran
aldebaran.desc: Aldebaran is a K5 III orange giant, the brightest star in Taurus, at about 20.4 parsecs (67 light-years) from the Sun. Its angular diameter of about 20 milliarcseconds corresponds to a radius of 45.1 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 62.7 million km. It has a mass slightly greater than that of the Sun, about 1.13 solar masses.

polare.name: Polaris
polare.desc: Polaris, the North Star (Polaris Aa), is a yellow supergiant and the nearest Cepheid variable, at about 137 parsecs (447 light-years). The CHARA interferometer measured a mean angular diameter of 3.143 milliarcseconds, equal to a radius of 46.3 solar radii and a diameter of about 64 million km. From the orbit of its companion, which lasts about 30 years, a mass of 5.13 solar masses is derived.

albireo-a.name: Albireo A
albireo-a.desc: Albireo A is the orange component of the famous double star in Cygnus, a bright K-type giant. The NPOI interferometer measured an angular diameter of 4.904 milliarcseconds, which corresponds to a radius of about 58.7 solar radii and a diameter of about 82 million km. It is not a single star: it has at least one close companion, with an orbital period of about 122 years.

rigel.name: Rigel
rigel.desc: Rigel is a B8 Ia blue supergiant, the brightest star in Orion. The angular diameter of 2.75 milliarcseconds, measured with the CHARA interferometer, corresponds to a radius of 78.9 ± 7.4 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 110 million km. It is one of the nearest stars destined to explode as a type II supernova.

distanza-terra-sole.name: Earth–Sun distance
distanza-terra-sole.desc: The mean distance between the Earth and the Sun corresponds to one astronomical unit, which since 2012 the International Astronomical Union has fixed by definition at exactly 149,597,870,700 metres, that is, about 149.6 million km. The light of the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 19 seconds to cover it.

gacrux.name: Gacrux
gacrux.desc: Gacrux (Gamma Crucis) is the M3.5 III red giant at the top of the Southern Cross, at about 27 parsecs (88 light-years) from the Sun. The angular diameter of 24.7 milliarcseconds corresponds to a radius of about 73 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 100 million km. It is one of the red giants closest to us.

deneb.name: Deneb
deneb.desc: Deneb is an A2 white supergiant, the brightest star in Cygnus. Its distance is poorly known and with it the radius: spectroscopic analysis at 802 parsecs gives 203 ± 17 solar radii (about 280 million km in diameter), while the NPOI angular diameter with the Hipparcos parallax (about 433 parsecs) gives about 117 solar radii. In both cases it is one of the intrinsically most luminous stars visible to the naked eye, with about 196,000 times the luminosity of the Sun in the highest estimate.

enif.name: Enif
enif.desc: Enif (Epsilon Pegasi) is a K2 orange supergiant, the brightest star in Pegasus, at about 211 parsecs (690 light-years). The NPOI interferometer measured an angular diameter of 8.038 milliarcseconds, which corresponds to a radius of about 183 solar radii and a diameter of about 254 million km. Its luminosity is about 8,500 times that of the Sun.

r-doradus.name: R Doradus
r-doradus.desc: R Doradus is a variable red giant at about 55 parsecs (180 light-years), the asymptotic giant branch star nearest to us. Its infrared angular diameter, 51.2 milliarcseconds, corresponds to a diameter of about 415 million km, around 300 times that of the Sun. In 2024 ALMA imaged its surface, following bubbles of hot gas 75 times the size of the Sun that surface and sink within a month.

pistol-star.name: Pistol Star
pistol-star.desc: The Pistol Star is a luminous blue variable in the Quintuplet Cluster, near the centre of the Milky Way. Atmosphere models assign it a radius of 306 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 430 million km, and a luminosity of about 1.6 million times that of the Sun. The dust of the Galactic plane hides it from visible light: it is studied in the infrared.

la-superba.name: La Superba
la-superba.desc: La Superba (Y Canum Venaticorum) is a J-type carbon star in Canes Venatici, of a very deep red. Its radius is not measured directly: from a luminosity of about 6,200 times that of the Sun and a temperature of about 2,760 K, about 340 solar radii are derived at 218 parsecs, that is, about 480 million km in diameter, and up to about 430 solar radii if the distance is 272 parsecs. It is surrounded by a shell of gas and dust expelled in the past.

s-doradus.name: S Doradus
s-doradus.desc: S Doradus is a luminous blue variable in the Large Magellanic Cloud, the prototype of the class of variables that bears its name. Its radius really does change over time: from about 100 solar radii at minimum light to about 380 at maximum, that is, from about 140 to 530 million km in diameter. Meanwhile the surface temperature drops from about 20,000 to 9,000 K.

v838-monocerotis.name: V838 Monocerotis
v838-monocerotis.desc: V838 Monocerotis is the star that in 2002 produced a red nova eruption, attributed to the merger of two stars. At the end of 2004 its radius was estimated at 1,570 ± 400 solar radii, then the star contracted: 750 ± 200 solar radii in 2014 and about 464 in a 2021 model. The value shown, about 650 million km in diameter, corresponds to this last estimate.

v382-carinae.name: V382 Carinae
v382-carinae.desc: V382 Carinae (HD 96918) is a yellow hypergiant in the constellation Carina. A 2026 study, which recalculates its distance with Gaia data, derives from an angular diameter of 2.18 milliarcseconds a radius of 616 ± 69 solar radii, that is, a diameter of about 857 million km. Earlier estimates ranged from 485 to 700 solar radii.

distanza-giove-sole.name: Jupiter–Sun distance
distanza-giove-sole.desc: Jupiter orbits at a mean distance from the Sun of about 778.5 million km, equal to 5.2 astronomical units. The distance varies from 740.6 million km at perihelion to 816.4 million km at aphelion. A full orbit lasts 4,332.6 days, almost 12 Earth years.

antares.name: Antares
antares.desc: Antares is a red supergiant in the constellation Scorpius. The VLTI interferometer measured its angular diameter, 37.4 milliarcseconds, which with the parallax gives a radius of 680 solar radii, equal to 3.2 astronomical units. The diameter is therefore about 946 million km: in place of the Sun, the star would extend beyond the orbit of Mars.

v354-cephei.name: V354 Cephei
v354-cephei.desc: V354 Cephei is a red supergiant in the constellation Cepheus. Estimates of its radius are very discordant: about 690 solar radii with the lowest published luminosity, 76,000 times that of the Sun, and 1,520 solar radii according to a 2005 study that credited it with a luminosity almost five times greater. The value shown, about 950 million km in diameter, corresponds to the lowest estimate.

terametro.name: Terametre
terametro.desc: The terametre (Tm) is 10^12 metres, that is, a billion kilometres: the SI prefix tera stands for a factor of a thousand billion. It corresponds to about 6.7 astronomical units, almost seven times the mean distance between the Earth and the Sun. Light takes about 56 minutes to travel it.

betelgeuse.name: Betelgeuse
betelgeuse.desc: Betelgeuse is a red supergiant in the constellation Orion. A 2020 study estimates its radius at 764 solar radii, with a margin from about 700 to 880, and its distance at 168 parsecs: the diameter is about 1.06 billion km. After the Great Dimming of 2019–2020, in 2025 the Gemini North telescope revealed a probable companion star in a very tight orbit.

uy-scuti.name: UY Scuti
uy-scuti.desc: UY Scuti is a red supergiant in the constellation Scutum. In 2013 interferometry with the VLTI assigned it a radius of 1,708 ± 192 solar radii, adopting a distance of 2,900 parsecs. With the nearer distance derived from Gaia data, about 1,870 parsecs, a 2024 catalogue reduces it to about 909 solar radii, that is, 1.26 billion km in diameter.

ky-cygni.name: KY Cygni
ky-cygni.desc: KY Cygni is a red supergiant in the constellation Cygnus. Its radius is not measured directly and estimates range from about 1,000 to 2,850 solar radii, depending on the luminosity adopted. The value shown, about 1,035 solar radii or 1.44 billion km in diameter, lies at the lower end of this range.

vv-cephei-a.name: VV Cephei A
vv-cephei-a.desc: VV Cephei A is the red supergiant of an eclipsing binary system with a period of about 20.3 years. Its radius has been estimated between 600 and 1,800 solar radii, because the semi-transparent outer atmosphere makes the eclipses begin and end gradually. The value shown corresponds to about 1,050 solar radii, or 1.46 billion km in diameter.

mu-cephei.name: Mu Cephei
mu-cephei.desc: Mu Cephei, Herschel's Garnet Star, is a red supergiant in the constellation Cepheus. Radius estimates depend on the distance, still poorly known: 972 ± 228 solar radii in a 2019 study that adopts 641 parsecs, 1,420 in a 2005 study. The value shown follows the most recent estimate, about 1.35 billion km in diameter.

vy-canis-majoris.name: VY Canis Majoris
vy-canis-majoris.desc: VY Canis Majoris is a red supergiant in the constellation Canis Major, wrapped in an extended envelope of dust. The VLTI interferometer measured the angular diameter of its photosphere, 11.3 ± 0.3 milliarcseconds, which corresponds to a radius of 1,420 ± 120 solar radii. The diameter is therefore about 1.98 billion km.

woh-g64.name: WOH G64
woh-g64.desc: WOH G64 is a red supergiant in the Large Magellanic Cloud, surrounded by a thick torus of dust. In 2009 its radius was calculated at 1,540 solar radii, but around 2014 the star changed and a study published in 2026 indicates a current radius of about 800 solar radii, the value shown here. Spectra from 2024–2025 show that it is still a red supergiant, so its nature and size remain debated.

stephenson-2-18.name: Stephenson 2-18
stephenson-2-18.desc: Stephenson 2-18, also called DFK 1, is a red supergiant associated with the cluster Stephenson 2 (RSGC2). The radius of about 2,150 solar radii is not a measurement: it is calculated from a luminosity of about 437,000 times that of the Sun and a temperature of 3,200 K estimated in 2012. A 2026 study lowers the luminosity to 321,000 ± 115,000 times that of the Sun, which corresponds to about 1,840 solar radii, and notes that the star may not belong to the cluster.

distanza-nettuno-sole.name: Neptune–Sun distance
distanza-nettuno-sole.desc: Neptune, the outermost planet, orbits at a mean distance from the Sun of about 4.5 billion km, equal to about 30.1 astronomical units. Its orbit is almost circular: the distance varies only from 4.47 to 4.56 billion km. A full orbit takes 60,189 days, almost 165 Earth years.

distanza-plutone-sole.name: Pluto–Sun distance
distanza-plutone-sole.desc: Pluto orbits at a mean distance from the Sun of about 5.9 billion km, that is, about 39.5 astronomical units. Its orbit is very elongated: the distance varies from 4.43 billion km at perihelion to 7.30 billion km at aphelion. A full orbit lasts 90,560 days, about 248 Earth years.

fascia-di-kuiper.name: Kuiper belt
fascia-di-kuiper.desc: The Kuiper belt is a doughnut-shaped region populated by icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune. The main part runs from about 30 to about 50 astronomical units from the Sun, so it measures about 100 AU (15 billion km) from one side to the other. Beyond its edge the scattered disc overlaps it, which according to NASA reaches almost 1,000 AU.

voyager-1.name: Voyager 1
voyager-1.desc: Voyager 1, launched on 5 September 1977, is the human-made object farthest from Earth. NASA has calculated that on 18 November 2026 it will reach the milestone of one light-day of distance, that is, 25.902 billion km: at that distance a radio signal takes 24 hours to reach the probe. In August 2012 it was the first probe to enter interstellar space.

giorno-luce.name: Light-day
giorno-luce.desc: The light-day is the distance that light travels in a vacuum in 24 hours: about 25.9 billion kilometres, equal to about 173 astronomical units. According to NASA the Voyager 1 probe reaches this distance from Earth on 18 November 2026, a milestone never reached by any other human-made object.

eliopausa.name: Heliopause
eliopausa.desc: The heliopause is the outer boundary of the heliosphere, the bubble of particles and magnetic fields generated by the Sun. Voyager 1 crossed it on 25 August 2012 at about 122 astronomical units from the Sun, that is, about 18 billion km, and Voyager 2 followed on 5 November 2018. The diameter shown here, about 240 AU, is twice that distance; the two Voyagers remain the only human-made objects to have reached interstellar space.

m87.name: M87*
m87.desc: M87* is the supermassive black hole at the centre of the galaxy Messier 87, 55 million light-years from Earth. The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration estimated its mass at 6.5 billion solar masses, with an uncertainty of 0.7 billion. In 2019 it became the first black hole of which an image was obtained.

afelio-della-cometa-hale-bopp.name: Aphelion of Comet Hale-Bopp
afelio-della-cometa-hale-bopp.desc: Comet Hale-Bopp, discovered on 23 July 1995 and at perihelion on 1 April 1997, follows a very elongated orbit. JPL's orbital elements put its aphelion at about 354 astronomical units from the Sun, over ten times the distance of Neptune. The nucleus has a diameter of about 60 km.

afelio-di-sedna.name: Aphelion of Sedna
afelio-di-sedna.desc: Sedna is a trans-Neptunian body with a very elongated orbit, which takes about 11,000 years to complete. Its aphelion is at about 936 astronomical units according to recent studies, but JPL's heliocentric orbital elements give about 1,010 AU: the value depends on the reference frame and on the epoch of the calculation. Sedna is approaching perihelion, at about 76 AU, which it will reach in 2075–2076.

buco-nero-del-cosmic-horseshoe.name: Cosmic Horseshoe black hole
buco-nero-del-cosmic-horseshoe.desc: Ultramassive black hole at the centre of the lensing galaxy in the Cosmic Horseshoe system, about 5 billion light-years away. A 2025 study estimates its mass at about 36 billion solar masses by combining gravitational lensing and the motion of stars, with a range between about 30 and 43 billion plus a further systematic uncertainty. The authors list it among the ten most massive black holes known.

ton-618.name: TON 618
ton-618.desc: TON 618 is a very luminous quasar powered by an ultramassive black hole. The mass is not measured directly but estimated from the width of the Hβ line in the spectrum: 66 billion solar masses according to a 2004 study, about 41 billion according to a 2019 recalibration. The diameter shown corresponds to the higher estimate.

nebulosa-stingray.name: Stingray Nebula
nebulosa-stingray.desc: The Stingray Nebula (Hen 3-1357) is considered the youngest known planetary nebula: its gas began to glow only in the 1980s. The diameter depends on the distance, estimated between 0.83 and 5.6 kiloparsecs, and therefore ranges from about 2 × 10^14 to 1.5 × 10^15 m. Hubble images from 1996 and 2016 show that in twenty years it has faded drastically.

petametro.name: Petametre
petametro.desc: The petametre (Pm) is 10^15 metres, that is, a thousand billion kilometres: the SI prefix peta stands for a factor of 10^15. It corresponds to about a tenth of a light-year (0.106) and to about 6,700 astronomical units. Light takes almost 39 days to travel it.

distanza-proxima-alfa-centauri-a.name: Proxima–Alpha Centauri A distance
distanza-proxima-alfa-centauri-a.desc: Proxima Centauri is gravitationally bound to the pair of stars Alpha Centauri A and B, as velocity measurements published in 2017 showed. It is now near the farthest point of its orbit, at about 13,000 astronomical units from the pair, and at periastron it comes down to about 4,300 AU. A full orbit lasts about 550,000 years.

nebulosa-occhio-di-gatto.name: Cat's Eye Nebula
nebulosa-occhio-di-gatto.desc: The Cat's Eye Nebula (NGC 6543) is a planetary nebula in the constellation Draco, among the most complex known. The bright inner core measures 16.1 arcseconds which, at the distance of 1001 ± 269 parsecs derived from its expansion, corresponds to about 2.4 × 10^15 m, with an uncertainty of about 27%. The same study assigns it an age of about 1000 years.

hamburger-di-gomez.name: Gomez's Hamburger
hamburger-di-gomez.desc: Gomez's Hamburger (IRAS 18059-3211) is a young star hidden by a large protoplanetary disc seen almost edge-on: the dark dust is the patty, the reflected light the two buns. ALMA observations published in 2026 give the gas disc a radius of about 900 astronomical units, so a diameter of about 2.7 × 10^14 m, at a revised distance of 139 ± 24 parsecs. With the distance of 250 parsecs used previously the disc would come out almost twice as large.

nebulosa-clessidra.name: Hourglass Nebula
nebulosa-clessidra.desc: The Hourglass Nebula (MyCn 18) is a young planetary nebula in the constellation Musca, about 8000 light-years away. The hourglass measures 18 arcseconds from pole to pole, equal to about 6.5 × 10^15 m at the usual distance of 2.4 kiloparsecs, or 8.6 × 10^15 m if the distance is 3.2 kiloparsecs. In 1996 Hubble revealed its hourglass shape with walls incised by thin arcs.

nebulosa-blinking.name: Blinking Nebula
nebulosa-blinking.desc: The Blinking Nebula (NGC 6826, Caldwell 15) is a planetary nebula in Cygnus: through a telescope it seems to vanish when you stare at the central star and reappear when you look away. According to NASA it is about 2200 light-years away, about a thousand years old and less than half a light-year wide. The outer shell measures 31 × 27 arcseconds, so from about 3 × 10^15 m to over 7 × 10^15 m depending on the adopted distance.

nebulosa-homunculus.name: Homunculus Nebula
nebulosa-homunculus.desc: The Homunculus Nebula is the two-lobed shell of gas and dust expelled by the star Eta Carinae during the eruption of 1843, when for a time it became the second brightest star in the sky. According to NASA it measures about two thirds of a light-year along its major axis, that is, around 6 × 10^15 m. The name, given by Enrique Gaviola in 1950, comes from the appendages that vaguely resemble a head and feet.

nebulosa-ngc-2392.name: NGC 2392 Nebula
nebulosa-ngc-2392.desc: NGC 2392 is a planetary nebula in Gemini, discovered by William Herschel in 1787: an inner bubble driven by the wind of the dying star and an outer shell adorned with comet-shaped filaments. The outer shell has a radius of 23 arcseconds and, at 1.4 kiloparsecs, a diameter of about 9.6 × 10^15 m, but distance estimates range from 1.28 to 1.8 kiloparsecs. In 2020 NASA announced that it would no longer use the nickname "Eskimo Nebula".

anno-luce.name: Light-year
anno-luce.desc: The light-year is the distance that light travels in a vacuum in a year: about 9,461 billion kilometres, or 9.46 × 10^15 metres. With the Julian year of 365.25 days the exact value is 9,460,730,472,580.8 km. It equals about 63,240 astronomical units.

nebulosa-uovo-marcio.name: Rotten Egg Nebula
nebulosa-uovo-marcio.desc: The Rotten Egg Nebula, also called the Calabash Nebula or OH 231.8+4.2, is gas expelled by a dying star about 5000 light-years away, in the constellation Puppis. It is 1.4 light-years long, about 1.3 × 10^16 m, and owes its nickname to the abundance of sulphur. According to NASA it will become a complete planetary nebula in about 1000 years.

nebulosa-formica.name: Ant Nebula
nebulosa-formica.desc: The Ant Nebula (Menzel 3) is a bipolar planetary nebula in the constellation Norma: two lobes of gas expelled by a dying Sun-like star, which together recall the head and thorax of an ant. On the sky it is about 1 arcminute long. NASA places it at about 3000 light-years, which gives 1.6 light-years (1.5 × 10^16 m), while the ESA/Hubble entry gives 8000 light-years, which would bring the length to about 2.2 × 10^16 m.

nebulosa-boomerang.name: Boomerang Nebula
nebulosa-boomerang.desc: The Boomerang Nebula is a young planetary nebula in Centaurus, about 5000 light-years away. Its rapidly expanding gas has cooled to about 1 kelvin, less than the cosmic microwave background, which makes it the coldest object known in the Universe. ALMA observations show that the ultracold outflow extends for almost four light-years, about 3.6 × 10^16 m.

nebulosa-anello.name: Ring Nebula
nebulosa-anello.desc: The Ring Nebula (M57, NGC 6720) is a planetary nebula in Lyra, about 2000–2500 light-years from Earth. According to NASA the main ring measures about 1 light-year, that is, about 9.5 × 10^15 m. In 2023 the Webb telescope showed about 20,000 dense globules rich in molecular hydrogen in it.

nube-di-oort.name: Oort Cloud
nube-di-oort.desc: The Oort Cloud is a theorised spherical shell of icy bodies surrounding the Solar System and is thought to be the source of long-period comets. According to NASA the inner edge lies between 2,000 and 5,000 astronomical units from the Sun and the outer one between 10,000 and 100,000 AU; the diameter shown here uses the farthest limit. At its current speed Voyager 1 will take about 300 years to reach it and perhaps 30,000 to leave it.

parsec.name: Parsec
parsec.desc: The parsec (pc) is the distance unit most used by astronomers for stars and galaxies: it is about 3.0857 × 10^16 metres, that is, 3.26 light-years. It corresponds to about 206,265 astronomical units, and since 2015 a resolution of the International Astronomical Union has fixed its exact value from the astronomical unit.

nebulosa-testa-di-cavallo.name: Horsehead Nebula
nebulosa-testa-di-cavallo.desc: The Horsehead, catalogued as Barnard 33, is a dark cloud of dust and gas in the constellation Orion, visible because it stands out against the red glow of the hydrogen behind it. According to NASA it is about 5 light-years tall. Estimates of its distance range from 1,300 to 1,600 light-years depending on the source.

distanza-sole-proxima.name: Sun–Proxima distance
distanza-sole-proxima.desc: Proxima Centauri is a red dwarf and is the star closest to the Sun: it is 1.295 parsecs away, that is, about 4.2 light-years or 40,000 billion km. Its luminosity is about 0.1% of the Sun's, so it cannot be seen with the naked eye. Since 2016 it has been known that at least one planet, Proxima b, orbits it.

pilastri-della-creazione.name: Pillars of Creation
pilastri-della-creazione.desc: The Pillars of Creation are columns of cold gas and dust in the heart of the Eagle Nebula, eroded by the ultraviolet radiation of young nearby stars. They are 4 to 5 light-years tall. Made famous by a Hubble Space Telescope image of 1995, they were imaged in the infrared by the Webb telescope in 2022.

nebulosa-elica.name: Helix Nebula
nebulosa-elica.desc: The Helix Nebula (NGC 7293) is a planetary nebula, that is, the gas expelled by a Sun-like star at the end of its life. About 650 light-years away, in the constellation Aquarius, it is one of the planetary nebulae closest to Earth. The size depends on what is measured: the bright ring is almost 3 light-years wide, while the fainter outer halo exceeds 6 light-years.

nebulosa-bolla.name: Bubble Nebula
nebulosa-bolla.desc: The Bubble Nebula (NGC 7635) is a shell of gas inflated by the wind of a star 45 times more massive than the Sun, in the constellation Cassiopeia. NASA gives it a diameter of 7 light-years at a distance of 7,100 light-years, while ESA gives about 10 light-years at 8,000 light-years. It was discovered by William Herschel in 1787.

nebulosa-cono.name: Cone Nebula
nebulosa-cono.desc: The Cone Nebula is a column of cold gas and dust in a star-forming region (NGC 2264) in the constellation Monoceros, about 2,500 light-years away. It is 7 light-years long in all. The famous Hubble Space Telescope image shows only its upper part, for 2.5 light-years.

the-spire.name: The Spire
the-spire.desc: The Spire is a tower of cold gas and dust in the Eagle Nebula (M16), imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope in visible and infrared light. It is 9.5 light-years long, more than twice the distance between the Sun and the nearest star. The radiation of the young hot stars nearby illuminates and erodes it.

nebulosa-granchio.name: Crab Nebula
nebulosa-granchio.desc: The Crab Nebula (M1) is what remains of the supernova observed by Chinese astronomers in 1054, 6,500 light-years away in the constellation Taurus. Since then it has continued to expand and today is about 11 light-years wide. At its centre lies a pulsar, a rapidly rotating neutron star that powers the nebula.

nebulosa-di-orione.name: Orion Nebula
nebulosa-di-orione.desc: The Orion Nebula (M42) is a cloud of gas lit by young hot stars, visible to the naked eye below Orion's Belt. According to NASA it is the nearest large star-forming region to Earth: a 2007 parallax measurement places it at 414 parsecs, about 1,350 light-years. On the sky it covers about one degree, which at that distance corresponds to about 24 light-years.

nube-interstellare-locale.name: Local Interstellar Cloud
nube-interstellare-locale.desc: The Local Interstellar Cloud is the cloud of rarefied gas, mostly hydrogen and helium, that the Solar System is passing through. It is about 30 light-years wide and has a temperature of about 6,000 °C. According to NASA the Sun will soon leave it, on an astronomical scale.

nebulosa-grotta.name: Cave Nebula
nebulosa-grotta.desc: The Cave Nebula (Caldwell 9, Sh2-155) is an emission nebula in the constellation Cepheus, where new stars are forming. According to NASA it extends for about 40 light-years and is about 3,000 light-years away. It is diffuse and low in contrast, so much so that it was catalogued only in 1959 by Stewart Sharpless.

nebulosa-aquila.name: Eagle Nebula
nebulosa-aquila.desc: The Eagle Nebula (M16) is an emission nebula with a young star cluster, about 7,000 light-years away in the constellation Serpens. It measures about 70 by 55 light-years and contains the famous Pillars of Creation, which are only a small part of it. It was discovered in 1745 by the Swiss astronomer Jean-Philippe Loys de Chéseaux.

nebulosa-nord-america.name: North America Nebula
nebulosa-nord-america.desc: The North America Nebula (NGC 7000) is an emission nebula in the constellation Cygnus, whose shape recalls that of the continent. Measurements by the Gaia satellite place it at about 785 parsecs, that is, 2,560 light-years, and at this distance it is between 85 and 90 light-years wide. NASA's outreach pages still report about 50 light-years, calculated with the old distance of 1,500 light-years.

messier-14.name: Messier 14
messier-14.desc: Messier 14 is a globular cluster in the constellation Ophiuchus, about 29,000 light-years from Earth, containing over 150,000 stars. NOIRLab gives it a diameter of about 72 light-years, but a globular cluster has no sharp edge and other estimates reach about 100 light-years. It was discovered by Charles Messier in 1764.

esametro.name: Exametre
esametro.desc: The exametre (Em) is 10^18 metres: the SI prefix exa stands for a factor of 10^18. It corresponds to about 106 light-years, that is, about 32 parsecs. Light setting off today from one end of an exametre reaches the other after a little more than a century.

nebulosa-laguna.name: Lagoon Nebula
nebulosa-laguna.desc: The Lagoon Nebula (Messier 8) is a large cloud of gas and dust in Sagittarius in which new stars are born, visible even to the naked eye under dark skies. According to ESO it is about 5,000 light-years away and extends for about 100 light-years, but estimates vary: ESA/Hubble gives 55 light-years at a distance of 4,000. Inside it lies the young star cluster NGC 6530.

nebulosa-rosetta.name: Rosette Nebula
nebulosa-rosetta.desc: The Rosette Nebula is a cloud of emission gas in the constellation Monoceros, about 5,000 light-years from Earth. It has a diameter of about 130 light-years, more than five times that of the Orion Nebula. At its centre lies the young star cluster NGC 2244, whose massive stars have hollowed out the central cavity and make the gas glow.

omega-centauri.name: Omega Centauri
omega-centauri.desc: Omega Centauri is the most massive globular cluster of the Milky Way, with about 10 million stars at about 17,000 light-years from Earth. ESO gives it a diameter of about 150 light-years, while NASA gives about 450 light-years counting the more rarefied outer regions. In 2024 the motion of seven very fast stars observed by Hubble provided strong evidence of an intermediate-mass black hole at its centre.

nebulosa-della-carena.name: Carina Nebula
nebulosa-della-carena.desc: The Carina Nebula is a vast star-forming region of the Milky Way, about 7,500 light-years from Earth in the southern constellation Carina. According to ESO and ESA it extends for about 260 light-years, while NASA gives about 300. It hosts Eta Carinae, a stellar system more than a million times brighter than the Sun.

anello-di-barnard.name: Barnard's Loop
anello-di-barnard.desc: Barnard's Loop is an immense arc of glowing hydrogen that wraps around the constellation Orion, about 300 light-years wide and about 1,500 away. It is too faint to be seen with the naked eye and appears only in long-exposure photographs. It is thought to have been shaped by ancient supernova explosions and by the winds of the massive stars of the region.

messier-54.name: Messier 54
messier-54.desc: Messier 54 is a globular cluster about 90,000 light-years from Earth, the first discovered outside the Milky Way: it belongs to the Sagittarius Dwarf Elliptical Galaxy, whose nucleus it occupies. Its extent depends on the definition: the tidal radius of about 77 parsecs corresponds to a diameter of about 500 light-years, but half of the light comes from a sphere of just 6.4 parsecs radius. Messier discovered it in 1778 and only in 1994 was it understood that it is not part of our galaxy.

nebulosa-tarantola.name: Tarantula Nebula
nebulosa-tarantola.desc: The Tarantula Nebula (30 Doradus) lies in the Large Magellanic Cloud, about 170,000 light-years from Earth, and measures about 1,000 light-years from end to end. According to NASA it is the largest and brightest star-forming region in the Local Group and hosts the hottest and most massive stars known. Despite the distance it is visible to the naked eye from the southern hemisphere.

bolla-locale.name: Local Bubble
bolla-locale.desc: The Local Bubble is a cavity of rarefied gas about 1,000 light-years wide, inside which the Sun now sits. According to a study published in Nature in 2022 it was carved out by about 15 supernovae that exploded starting 14 million years ago. On its surface lie all the young star-forming regions near us.

leo-ii.name: Leo II
leo-ii.desc: Leo II is a dwarf spheroidal galaxy, a satellite of the Milky Way, about 233 kpc (760,000 light-years) from us. Its extent depends on the definition: the core radius is about 178 pc and the tidal radius about 632 pc, so the diameter ranges from about 360 to about 1,260 pc (1,200 to 4,100 light-years); the tidal one is shown here. Measurements indicate that it is dominated by dark matter.

getto-relativistico-di-m87.name: M87 relativistic jet
getto-relativistico-di-m87.desc: From the supermassive black hole at the centre of the elliptical galaxy M87 emerges a jet of extremely hot gas travelling at speeds close to that of light. The visible part of the jet is about 5,000 light-years long. Thirteen years of Hubble Space Telescope observations have shown that the plasma appears to move in a spiral along the jet.

nana-del-cane-maggiore.name: Canis Major Dwarf
nana-del-cane-maggiore.desc: The Canis Major overdensity is a group of stars near the Galactic plane, reported in 2003 among the red giants of the 2MASS catalogue and proposed as the remnant of a dwarf galaxy swallowed by the Milky Way. A measurement along the line of sight gives a half-light radius of about 0.94 kpc, that is, a diameter of about 6,000 light-years, with wide uncertainties. Its nature is disputed: according to other studies it is merely a warp of the outer disc of the Milky Way.

canes-venatici-i.name: Canes Venatici I
canes-venatici-i.desc: Canes Venatici I is a dwarf galaxy, a satellite of the Milky Way, discovered in 2006 in Sloan Digital Sky Survey data at a distance of about 220 kpc (720,000 light-years). The radius that encloses half of its light is about 550 pc, for a diameter of about 1,100 pc (3,600 light-years). The outer regions appear more extended and distorted, so the overall extent is larger and not well defined.

onda-di-radcliffe.name: Radcliffe Wave
onda-di-radcliffe.desc: The Radcliffe Wave is an undulating chain of star-forming gas clouds, about 2.7 kiloparsecs long, that is, about 9,000 light-years, which passes through the Sun's surroundings. It was described in Nature in January 2020 thanks to distances measured by the Gaia satellite and contains about three million solar masses of gas. Its shape is that of a damped wave that rises and falls up to about 500 light-years relative to the plane of the Milky Way.

nana-ellittica-del-sagittario.name: Sagittarius Dwarf Elliptical Galaxy
nana-ellittica-del-sagittario.desc: The Sagittarius Dwarf Elliptical Galaxy is a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way, about 26 kpc (86,000 light-years) from the Sun. Its main body measures about 450 arcminutes along the major axis, that is, about 3.4 kpc (11,000 light-years), but the edge is poorly defined because the Milky Way is tearing it apart. The stripped stars form tidal tails that extend for over 150 degrees across the sky.

piccola-nube-di-magellano.name: Small Magellanic Cloud
piccola-nube-di-magellano.desc: The Small Magellanic Cloud is a dwarf galaxy, a satellite of the Milky Way, in the southern constellation Tucana. Its apparent major diameter is 320 arcminutes, over 5 degrees, which at a distance of about 61 kpc (200,000 light-years) corresponds to about 5.7 kpc, that is, about 18,500 light-years. NASA gives a slightly greater distance, about 210,000 light-years.

ngc-3310.name: NGC 3310
ngc-3310.desc: NGC 3310 is a spiral galaxy in Ursa Major with intense star formation. Its apparent diameter of 3.1 arcminutes corresponds to about 12 kpc (38,000 light-years) at the mean distance of about 13 Mpc reported by NED. Distance estimates, however, range from about 11 to 19 Mpc, and NASA, which adopts 18 Mpc, gives a diameter of about 52,000 light-years.

grande-nube-di-magellano.name: Large Magellanic Cloud
grande-nube-di-magellano.desc: The Large Magellanic Cloud is a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way, classified as a Magellanic-type barred spiral, about 50 kpc (163,000 light-years) away. Its apparent major diameter is 645 arcminutes, almost 11 degrees, which at that distance corresponds to about 9.4 kpc, that is, about 30,600 light-years.

ngc-7714.name: NGC 7714
ngc-7714.desc: NGC 7714 is a spiral galaxy in the constellation Pisces, about 100 million light-years away, distorted by its interaction with the smaller companion NGC 7715. Its apparent diameter of 1.9 arcminutes corresponds to about 16 kpc, that is, between 50,000 and 55,000 light-years depending on the adopted distance. The two galaxies brushed past each other between 100 and 200 million years ago and are joined by a bridge of stars.

bolle-di-fermi.name: Fermi Bubbles
bolle-di-fermi.desc: The Fermi Bubbles are two enormous gamma-ray-emitting lobes that extend above and below the centre of the Milky Way. Each is about 25,000 light-years tall, for a total of 50,000 light-years, about half the diameter of the galaxy. They were discovered in 2010 in data from NASA's Fermi Space Telescope and might be the remnant of an ancient eruption of the central black hole.

galassia-occhio-nero.name: Black Eye Galaxy
galassia-occhio-nero.desc: The Black Eye Galaxy (M64) is a spiral in Coma Berenices, known for the band of dark dust beside the nucleus. According to NOIRLab it measures about 55,000 light-years in diameter; from the apparent diameter of 10 arcminutes and a distance of about 5.5 Mpc (18 million light-years) about 53,000 light-years are obtained. It contains two systems of gas and stars that rotate in opposite directions.

galassia-del-triangolo.name: Triangulum Galaxy
galassia-del-triangolo.desc: The Triangulum Galaxy (M33) is a spiral about 3 million light-years away, third in size in the Local Group after Andromeda and the Milky Way. According to ESA/Hubble it measures about 60,000 light-years in diameter and contains about 40 billion stars.

galassia-vortice.name: Whirlpool Galaxy
galassia-vortice.desc: The Whirlpool Galaxy (M51) is a spiral in Canes Venatici, interacting with the small companion NGC 5195. Its apparent diameter is 11.2 arcminutes, but the distance is uncertain: between about 23 and 31 million light-years depending on the source. This gives a diameter of about 77,000 light-years with the mean distance reported by NED, while NASA gives about 60,000 light-years.

via-lattea.name: Milky Way
via-lattea.desc: The Milky Way is the spiral galaxy in which the Sun lies, about 8 kpc (26,000 light-years) from the centre. The diameter of the stellar disc out to the isophote of 25 magnitudes per square arcsecond is estimated at 26.8 ± 1.1 kpc, that is, about 87,400 light-years. The most-quoted rounded value, also by NASA, is about 100,000 light-years.

galassia-sombrero.name: Sombrero Galaxy
galassia-sombrero.desc: The Sombrero Galaxy (M104) is a spiral seen almost edge-on in the constellation Virgo, with a large central bulge and a dark band of dust. The major diameter of 8.7 arcminutes, at a distance of 9.55 megaparsecs (about 31 million light-years), corresponds to about 79,000 light-years, but sources range from the 50,000 light-years given by ESA/Hubble to higher values depending on where the edge is placed. Hubble picks out almost 2,000 globular clusters in it, about ten times those of the Milky Way.

zettametro.name: Zettametre
zettametro.desc: The zettametre (Zm) is 10^21 metres: the SI prefix zetta stands for a factor of 10^21. It corresponds to about 105,700 light-years, that is, about 32,400 parsecs. It is a suitable unit for expressing the sizes of galaxies.

virgo-a.name: Virgo A
virgo-a.desc: Virgo A is the radio source associated with Messier 87, a giant elliptical galaxy of the Virgo Cluster about 54 million light-years away. The bright body measures about 130,000 light-years (ESA/Hubble gives 120,000), while the halo of stars reaches about a million light-years in diameter according to VLT measurements. The black hole at its centre is the first of which an image has been obtained, published in 2019 by the Event Horizon Telescope.

galassia-ruota-di-carro.name: Cartwheel Galaxy
galassia-ruota-di-carro.desc: The Cartwheel Galaxy is a ring galaxy about 500 million light-years away, in the constellation Sculptor. The outer ring, about 150,000 light-years wide, was born from a head-on collision with a smaller galaxy that passed through it. According to NASA it contains at least a few billion new stars and could enclose the whole Milky Way.

andromeda.name: Andromeda
andromeda.desc: Andromeda (M31) is the large spiral galaxy nearest to the Milky Way, at 2.5 million light-years. The visible disc has a major axis of about 190–200 arcminutes, that is, about 140,000–150,000 light-years, and on the sky it appears six times as wide as the full Moon. Its halo of rarefied gas is much more extended: Hubble traced it out to 1.3 million light-years from the galaxy.

galassia-girandola.name: Pinwheel Galaxy
galassia-girandola.desc: The Pinwheel Galaxy (M101) is a face-on spiral in Ursa Major, about 25 million light-years away. Its disc of stars, dust and gas measures 170,000 light-years, almost twice that of the Milky Way. Astronomers estimate that it contains at least a trillion stars.

ngc-1232.name: NGC 1232
ngc-1232.desc: NGC 1232 is a nearly face-on spiral galaxy in the constellation Eridanus, about 60 million light-years away. Its major axis of 7.4 arcminutes corresponds to about 130,000 light-years, a little more than the Milky Way. Chandra X-ray observations revealed in it a cloud of gas at 6 million degrees, a probable trace of a collision with a dwarf galaxy.

ngc-4889.name: NGC 4889
